Reference

The public names are importable from idtrack (idtrack.API, idtrack.HarmonizeFeatures, …) and are documented here under those names. The modules idtrack._<name> hold them; what is documented under a module path below (helper functions, constants, the graph’s value types) is used by the public classes and may change between versions.

Conversion and harmonization

class API(local_repository)[source]

Bases: object

Provide a high-level façade for building graphs and converting biological identifiers with IDTrack.

One API holds at most one loaded graph (one organism, one snapshot release). Once build_graph() has returned, the object holds no other state that changes between calls: every conversion is a function of its arguments and the graph, results are plain data (dict, list, str, int, bool, None; json.dumps works on every result), and the values returned by the list_* methods are copies. Arguments are validated before any search starts, and an invalid argument raises an error that names it and the accepted values.

Conversions only read the graph, so several threads may call convert_identifier() at once with the same answers as one; the search holds the interpreter lock, so threads do not run conversions in parallel. build_graph() prepares the new graph completely before it replaces the old one in a single assignment.

Bind the interface to a local repository used for data downloads and on-disk caches.

Constructing an API is inexpensive: the graph is loaded by build_graph().

Parameters:

local_repository (str) – Path to a writable directory where the package stores downloaded resources and graphs. The caller is responsible for ensuring the path exists and is accessible.

static _candidates(raw, explain)[source]

Flatten the answer of idtrack.Track.convert() into one record per (gene, target) pair.

This is the only place that reads the engine’s nested answer. The order of the engine (best first) is kept.

Parameters:

  • raw (dict) – The engine’s result: per gene its evidence, the_path and final_conversion with final_elements per target.

  • explain (bool) – Whether paths were requested.

Returns:

{"gene", "target", "entry_gene", "external_jump", "external_gap", "score", "path"}.

Return type:

list[dict]

build_graph(organism_name, snapshot_release, return_test=False)[source]

Load (or build) the graph of an organism and snapshot release and attach it to this object.

If the local repository holds the graph file, it is loaded from the file alone: no idtrack.DatabaseManager, no table and no network connection are needed (idtrack.GraphMaker.load_graph()). A file that holds another graph than the one asked for (another selection of external databases, another organism table, another format) is an error that names the difference and the way out (idtrack.GraphMismatchError), never a silent rebuild. Only if there is no file, the graph is built from Ensembl’s tables through a idtrack.DatabaseManager that ignores releases newer than snapshot_release, and saved. The new tracker replaces the previous one only when it is ready.

Parameters:

  • organism_name (str) – Canonical Ensembl species name, typically the output of resolve_organism().

  • snapshot_release (int) – Ensembl release anchoring this build. Data from later releases are ignored. The graph is built on the organism’s assemblies in their order of the organism table (idtrack.DB.assembly_mysqlport_priority): its primary assembly is the preferred one that has snapshot_release, and the ids of the other assemblies (earlier ones, and human GRCh37 beside GRCh38) are in the graph as ids to convert from.

  • return_test (bool) – Attach a idtrack.TrackTests (the graph’s self-tests, which read Ensembl’s tables and therefore always need a database manager) instead of a idtrack.Track.

Return type:

None

Nothing is computed in advance for conversions: a graph, built or read from its file, carries its graph-wide tables, and what a conversion reads is computed for the nodes of the query.

See also

get_database_manager(), idtrack.Track.

classify_multiple_conversion(matchings)[source]

Group batch-conversion results into bins for reporting.

Every result is in "input_identifiers" and in exactly one of the bins "matching_1_to_0" (not found, no conversion, or an error), "matching_1_to_1", "matching_1_to_n", "alternative_target_1_to_1" and "alternative_target_1_to_n" (the last two: no_target, the targets are Ensembl genes standing in for a missing id of the requested database). A result of "matching_1_to_1" is also in "changed_only_1_to_1" when its target is not the identifier it resolved to, and one of "matching_1_to_n" is also in "changed_only_1_to_n" when none of its targets is. “The identifier it resolved to” is graph_id, compared without the synonym_id:: prefix and, for Ensembl ids, without the version, so that a query without version or in another case that maps to itself is not “changed”.

Parameters:

matchings (list[dict[str, Any]]) – Results of convert_identifier_multiple() or convert_identifier().

Returns:

The bins named above.

Return type:

dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]

Raises:

ValueError – If a result has no target although none of no_corresponding, no_conversion or error is set (an internal error).

static configure_logger(level=None)[source]

Show the messages of idtrack on the console, at level and above.

Attaches one console handler (time, level, logger name, message) to the package logger "idtrack" and sets that logger’s level. Only idtrack’s loggers are affected: the root logger and the loggers of other libraries keep their handlers and levels. Calling it again changes the level and never adds a second handler. Applications that configure logging themselves can instead set logging.getLogger("idtrack").setLevel(...) and leave this method alone.

Parameters:

level (int | str | None) – Logging level (e.g. logging.INFO, "DEBUG"). None means logging.INFO.

Return type:

None

convert_identifier(identifier, from_release=None, to_release=None, final_database=None, strategy='best', explain=False, from_database=None)[source]

Convert one identifier to a target Ensembl release and database.

The identifier is resolved to a node of the graph (idtrack.TheGraph.resolve_name()): between the nodes the string can mean, one that exists at from_release (without one: at the last release of the graph) is taken before one that does not (with from_database: as an id of that database), and an Ensembl id is never passed over. An identifier exists at a release on the genome assembly that serves the release (a name that only human GRCh37, listed beside GRCh38, still carries does not exist today). Among those it is matched exactly (as a database wrote the identifier at the release it is read at), then ignoring letter case, then taking -, _ and . as one character, then without the version of a sequence accession, each step on names and then on synonyms before the next begins. How it matched is reported. idtrack.Track.convert(), which reads the identifier by the same rule, finds its Ensembl gene(s) at to_release and their ids in final_database. Every argument is validated before the search starts.

Parameters:

  • identifier (str) – Ensembl id (with or without version), symbol or other external id. Surrounding white space is ignored.

  • from_release (int | None) – Ensembl release at which identifier is read. If None, it is read at to_release when it is active there, otherwise at the latest release in which it is active. If a release is given at which the graph does not hold the identifier (a real id of that release that the graph’s selection of external databases lacks there, or a wrong release), the identifier is read by the same rule as without from_release, and the result says so: "from_release_fallback" is true, "from_release" is the release used and "from_release_given" the one given. (idtrack.Track.convert() itself is strict and raises idtrack.InactiveAtReleaseError.)

  • to_release (int | None) – Target Ensembl release; None means the graph’s snapshot release. Must be a release of the graph (graph_releases()).

  • final_database (str | None) – Database of the targets (valid_final_databases() of to_release, matched case-insensitively); None means "ensembl_gene".

  • strategy (Literal["all", "best"]) – "best" (default) keeps the best answer: one target, or the targets that are equal in all evidence ("tie" is then true); "all" keeps every target reached.

  • explain (bool) – Add "the_path", the edges by which each target was reached.

  • from_database (str | None) – The external database identifier is meant as (an id that names different things in two databases is then read in this one only); one of list_external_databases(). None (default) reads it in any database.

Returns:

Plain data (json.loads(json.dumps(r)) == r):

  • "query_id" (str): identifier as given.

  • "graph_id" (str | None): The graph node the identifier was read as (None: not found). For an Ensembl transcript or translation id without version this is its version of the starting release.

  • "match" (str | None): How the identifier matched "graph_id": "exact", "case", "separator", "version" (each also after "synonym:" for a synonym), or "version_newer_than_graph" (an Ensembl id with a version higher than all the graph holds, active at the graph’s last release: read as its latest version; see idtrack.TheGraph.resolve_name()); None when it is not in the graph.

  • "known_versions" (list[str]): Empty, except for an Ensembl id written with a version that the graph does not hold and that cannot be newer than the graph: such an id is not answered with another version’s gene ("no_corresponding" is true), and this lists the versions that exist.

  • "from_release" (int | None): The release at which the identifier was read: the argument when given and usable, otherwise the release the engine chose (None when nothing was read).

  • "from_release_inferred" (bool): The release was chosen by the engine, not given.

  • "from_release_given" (int | None), "from_release_fallback" (bool): The argument, and whether it was set aside because the graph does not hold the identifier at that release.

  • "from_databases" (list[str]): For an external id, the databases through which it was read at that release: every database that attaches it there to one of its genes, to the gene itself or to one of its transcripts or translations (with from_database: that database).

  • "to_release" (int), "strategy" (str): The arguments as used (to_release resolved).

  • "final_database" (str | None): The database of the values in "target_id": the requested one when a target in it was found, "ensembl_gene" when the genes reached have no id in it (no_target), None when nothing was found.

  • "target_id" (list[str]): The targets, in the order of "last_node", each once. One element for an unambiguous answer.

  • "last_node" (list[list[str]]): [ensembl_gene, target] for each target; the gene is the Ensembl gene at to_release through which the target was reached. The order is the engine’s, best first: with "all" the genes of the best answer lead, in the order in which "best" returns them, and the others follow by their evidence. The pairs of a tie are ordered by the mapping score of each to the gene the identifier was read as, then by gene id and target id.

  • "ambiguous" (bool): More than one target (a 1-to-n answer).

  • "tie" (bool): The best answer of this conversion is shared by several genes or targets that are equal in all evidence (with "best" these are the pairs returned). A tie is judged among the genes that have an id in the requested database: genes without one are not in the result ("no_target_genes"), so a symbol that two databases give to two genes is a tie when converted to Ensembl gene ids and one answer when converted to a database in which only one of the two genes has an id.

  • "alternative_locus_genes" (list[str]): Genes on alternative loci (haplotypes) and assembly patches, and LRG records, that the identifier also leads to, beside genes of the reference sequence: copies with stable ids of their own, which are not in "target_id". Empty when there is none, and when the copies are themselves the answer (nothing of the reference sequence was reached).

  • "no_corresponding" (bool): The identifier is not in the graph.

  • "no_conversion" (bool): It is in the graph, but no path to to_release exists (1-to-0).

  • "no_target" (bool): Genes were reached, but none has an id in the requested database; then "target_id" holds the Ensembl gene ids and "final_database" is "ensembl_gene".

  • "no_target_genes" (list[str]): Genes that were reached but have no id in the requested database while others have (they are not in "target_id"); otherwise empty.

  • "error" (None | dict): Always None here (errors raise); in convert_identifier_multiple() a per-query failure as {"type", "message"}.

  • "the_path" (list[dict]): Only with explain: for each pair of "last_node" (same order), {"ensembl_gene", "target_id", "entry_gene", "external_jump", "external_gap", "score", "edges"}: the gene the identifier was read as and from which this gene was reached, the number of bridges through external ids (0: Ensembl’s history only), the releases between leaving a gene and entering the next over those bridges, the product of Ensembl’s mapping scores, and the edges of the history walk and then of the final hop, as lists.

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

Raises:

  • TypeError – If identifier is not a string or a release is not an integer.

  • ValueError – If identifier is empty, a release is not one of the graph, final_database is not a database of the graph at to_release or strategy is not "best"/"all".

  • idtrack.SearchBudgetExceededError – If the search needs more than its budget (idtrack.Track.search_budget_states, idtrack.Track.search_budget_seconds).

  • RuntimeError – If no graph is loaded.

convert_identifier_multiple(identifier_list, from_release=None, to_release=None, final_database=None, strategy='best', explain=False, from_database=None, verbose=True, pbar_prefix='')[source]

Convert a batch of identifiers with the same arguments.

The arguments are validated once, before any conversion: a non-string or empty identifier raises with the positions of the offending items, as do invalid releases or databases. A failure that concerns one query only (a search that exceeds its budget) does not stop the batch: that item gets "error": {"type": ..., "message": ...}, empty targets and all three no_* flags false. Each distinct identifier is converted once; repeated identifiers get equal, independent copies of the result.

Parameters:

  • identifier_list (list[str]) – Identifiers to convert.

  • from_release (int | None) – See convert_identifier().

  • to_release (int | None) – See convert_identifier().

  • final_database (str | None) – See convert_identifier().

  • strategy (Literal["all", "best"]) – See convert_identifier().

  • explain (bool) – See convert_identifier().

  • from_database (str | None) – See convert_identifier().

  • verbose (bool) – Show a tqdm progress bar. Defaults to True.

  • pbar_prefix (str) – Label of the progress bar.

Returns:

One result per input identifier, in input order, each of the shape returned by convert_identifier().

Return type:

list[dict[str, Any]]

Raises:

  • TypeError – If identifier_list is not a list or tuple, or holds non-strings (positions named).

  • ValueError – If it holds empty strings (positions named) or an argument is invalid.

infer_identifier_source(id_list, mode='assembly_ensembl_release', report_only_winner=True)[source]

Infer the origins (database, assembly, release) that best explain a list of identifiers.

Each identifier found in the graph counts once for every origin in which it exists (idtrack.TheGraph.trios(), read for the given identifiers only). Identifiers not in the graph are counted and logged, not used. A string is read as the node it means at the last release of the graph (idtrack.TheGraph.resolve_name()): the release of the list is what is asked for, so no other release can be named; a string that meant one identifier once and means another today counts for today’s.

Parameters:

  • id_list (list[str]) – Identifiers (strings).

  • mode (str) – Granularity of an origin: "complete" → [database, assembly, release], "ensembl_release" → release, "assembly" → assembly, "assembly_ensembl_release" (default) → [assembly, release].

  • report_only_winner (bool) – True (default) returns every origin with the highest count (all origins tied for first place, sorted: e.g. all releases of the span in which the identifiers exist); False returns every origin with its count, by descending count, then origin.

Returns:

With report_only_winner, the sorted list of best origins; otherwise [origin, count] pairs.

Return type:

list

Raises:

  • ValueError – If mode is unknown, or none of the identifiers is in the graph.

  • TypeError – If an identifier is not a string.

class HarmonizeFeatures(project_name, data_h5ad_dict, project_local_repository, idtrack_local_repository, target_ensembl_release, final_database=None, organism_name=None, graph_last_ensembl_release=None, source_releases=None, source_databases=None, api=None, verbose_level=2, converted_id_column='converted_id')[source]

Bases: object

Convert the features of several single-cell datasets to one Ensembl release and merge the datasets.

For every dataset, each feature name (Ensembl gene id with or without version, symbol or other external id) is converted with idtrack.API.convert_identifier_multiple() to its Ensembl gene at target_ensembl_release. The conversion of a dataset depends only on that dataset (its feature names and its source_releases and source_databases entries), never on the other datasets.

Output features. Each converted gene is one feature, named by the gene id at the target release (with version); its final-database name (default: the organism’s symbol database) is in the column named after the final database. That name is a property of the gene, not of the query: the gene’s ids in the final database at the target release (idtrack.Track.gene_to_database(): read from the gene, no search), the first in sorted order when there are several (the others in "<final database>_alternatives"). A gene without an id in the final database keeps the gene id as its feature name and a missing final-database name (status "converted_no_final_id"): the final-database column never holds an Ensembl id. Features that are not converted keep their input name; no feature is dropped silently. Every output feature has, in var:

  • "idtrack_status": "converted", "converted_no_final_id", "merged", "merged_no_final_id" (with merge="sum", the sum of several input features), "unconverted_merge_partner" (with merge="flag", an input feature that shares its gene with others), "unconverted_ambiguous" (several genes), "unconverted_no_conversion" (in the graph, but no gene at the target release), "unconverted_not_in_graph" or "unconverted_error" (the conversion of this feature raised an error that concerns it alone, a search over its budget);

  • "idtrack_reason": why (missing for a plain conversion; for a feature that the graph does not hold at its dataset’s source release and that was therefore read at another release, that release);

  • "Query ID": the input name(s), ";"-joined for a merged feature;

  • "matching_ensembl_gene": the gene (also for a merge partner; missing for the other unconverted features).

Several input features of one dataset on one gene (an Ensembl merge, or two aliases): with merge="sum" (right for counts) they become one feature whose values in X and every layer are the sum of theirs; with merge="flag" (default, for normalised data, where a sum has no meaning) the feature that names the gene itself (its stable id or one of its final-database names, ignoring version and case) becomes the gene’s feature, and the others keep their input names with status "unconverted_merge_partner" (if none or several name the gene, all keep their names and the gene has no feature). Rows that a merge sums carry a var value only where all their input features agree (missing otherwise), and varm/varp are left out of a dataset in which features were summed.

An unconverted input name that equals a converted feature’s name (in the dataset, or in another dataset when merging) is renamed "unconverted:<name>", so that converted and unconverted measurements never share a row.

Result cache. The conversions of each dataset are stored in project_local_repository as one JSON file per dataset (written to a temporary file and renamed). A stored file is used only if it was written by the same idtrack version for the same feature names, organism, final database, target and source release, graph snapshot and graph (the graph file’s name, size and modification time, or the loaded graph’s metadata when api is given); an unreadable or mismatching file is recomputed and replaced.

Parameters:

  • project_name (str) – Label used in log messages and cache file names.

  • data_h5ad_dict (dict[str, str]) – {dataset name: path of an .h5ad file}; at least one.

  • project_local_repository (str) – Writable folder for the result cache (created if missing).

  • idtrack_local_repository (str) – idtrack’s local repository holding the graph.

  • target_ensembl_release (int) – Ensembl release all features are converted to; a release of the graph.

  • final_database (Optional[str]) – Database of the feature names in the output (e.g. "HGNC Symbol"). Defaults to the organism’s first symbol database (idtrack.DB.symbol_databases: HGNC Symbol for human, MGI Symbol for mouse, VGNC Symbol for pig and the macaques).

  • organism_name (Optional[str]) – Organism, as an Ensembl species name (e.g. "homo_sapiens") or any query idtrack.API.resolve_organism() accepts. If None, it is read from the graph files in idtrack_local_repository, which must then hold graphs of exactly one organism.

  • graph_last_ensembl_release (Optional[int]) – Snapshot release of the graph. If None, the newest graph of the organism in idtrack_local_repository (built by idtrack.API.build_graph()) is used, or the latest Ensembl release of the organism when there is none.

  • source_releases (Optional[dict[str, int]]) – The Ensembl release each dataset was annotated with, by dataset name. A dataset with a release is converted with from_release; a feature that the graph does not hold at that release is read where the graph holds it (the rule without a release, below), and its "idtrack_reason" says so. Without a release, each feature is read at the target release if it is active there, else at the latest release in which it is active.

  • source_databases (Optional[dict[str, str]]) – The external database the feature names of a dataset are ids of, by dataset name ({"study_a": "HGNC Symbol"}; one of idtrack.API.list_external_databases()). A dataset with a database is converted with from_database: every feature is read as an id of that database, so a symbol that another database gives to another gene is not a tie, and a feature that is no id of that database (an Ensembl id among symbols) is not converted. Without one, nothing is assumed about where a name comes from: a name that two databases give to two genes stands for both (status "unconverted_ambiguous") when both genes have a name in final_database; a tie is judged among the genes that can be named there, so when only one of the two has a name in it, the feature is converted to that gene. Nothing is inferred from the names on the caller’s behalf.

  • api (Optional[idtrack.API]) – An idtrack.API with the graph already loaded, to use instead of loading the graph again. Without it, the harmonizer loads the graph only if some dataset is not in the result cache, and releases it when the conversions are done.

  • verbose_level (Literal[0, 1, 2, 3]) – 0 shows nothing, 1 progress bars, 2 also a summary of each dataset’s conversions (logged at INFO by the "idtrack" loggers; see idtrack.API.configure_logger()), 3 also debug messages. The harmonizer never configures logging itself.

  • converted_id_column (str) – Name of the merged final-database column of unify_multiple_anndatas().

feature_names

The feature names of each dataset, in file order.

Type:

dict[str, list[str]]

matchings

The conversion of each feature of each dataset (results of idtrack.API.convert_identifier(), plain data).

Type:

dict[str, list[dict]]

gene_names

Per dataset, the final-database names of each gene reached.

Type:

dict[str, dict[str, list[str]]]

Validate the arguments, read the feature names and convert every feature of every dataset.

Everything that can be checked without the graph is checked before any conversion starts (the arguments, the files, the feature names, the project folder). The conversions then run, or are read from the result cache; this is the long part (minutes for large datasets when nothing is cached).

Parameters:

  • project_name (str) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • data_h5ad_dict (dict[str, str]) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • project_local_repository (str) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • idtrack_local_repository (str) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • target_ensembl_release (int) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • final_database (Optional[str]) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • organism_name (Optional[str]) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • graph_last_ensembl_release (Optional[int]) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • source_releases (Optional[dict[str, int]]) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • source_databases (Optional[dict[str, str]]) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • api (Optional[idtrack.API]) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • verbose_level (Literal[0, 1, 2, 3]) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • converted_id_column (str) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

Raises:

ValueError – If verbose_level is not 0 to 3; if data_h5ad_dict is empty, names a missing file or a dataset whose feature names are empty, not strings or repeated; if source_releases or source_databases names an unknown dataset; if a release is not an integer or a source database not a string, or target_ensembl_release is after the graph snapshot; if organism_name is None and the graphs in idtrack_local_repository do not name exactly one organism; if final_database is None and the organism declares no symbol database; and the errors of idtrack.API.convert_identifier_multiple() (e.g. a release or database not of the graph).

unify_multiple_anndatas(mode='union', obs_join='outer', obs_columns_to_keep=None, numeric_var_columns=None, numeric_obs_columns=None, handle_anndata_key='handle_anndata', merge='flag', keep_unconverted=True)[source]

Merge the harmonised datasets of data_h5ad_dict into one AnnData.

Each dataset is harmonised with feature_harmonizer() (with merge and keep_unconverted) and all are concatenated along the cells in one anndata.concat(). A feature is the same feature in two datasets when it has the same name: a converted gene id, or the same unconverted input name (an unconverted name equal to another dataset’s converted gene id is renamed "unconverted:<name>" first). By default nothing is lost, and values are never rewritten: text stays text, numbers stay numbers, and where a dataset has no value the result holds a missing value of the column’s kind (NaN for floats and text, pd.NA in a nullable integer or boolean column, NaT for times, a missing category for categoricals), never a placeholder string.

  • Features. "union" (default) keeps every feature of any dataset; a dataset that lacks a feature gets zeros for it in X and in every layer. "intersect" keeps the features present in every dataset.

  • .obs. obs_join="outer" (default) keeps every obs column of any dataset; in the cells of a dataset without the column it is missing (see above; an integer or boolean column becomes the nullable Int/ boolean dtype so that it can hold the missing values). obs_join="inner" keeps only the columns every dataset has. obs_columns_to_keep, if given, selects among the joined columns (in its order); a name that no dataset has, or (with "inner") that not every dataset has, raises ValueError naming it. Columns in numeric_obs_columns are converted to float (missing values allowed); other text columns become categorical (values unchanged). The column handle_anndata_key records the dataset of each cell (categorical, in the order of data_h5ad_dict), and cells are named f"{handle}_{cell}".

  • .var. converted_id_column holds the final-database name of each feature (missing for features without one), "matching_ensembl_gene" its gene. Per dataset: f"{column}_{handle}" for "Query ID", "idtrack_status" and "idtrack_reason" (missing where the dataset lacks the feature). In "union" mode also f"{converted_id_column}_{handle}" and an integer "intersection" column (1 if the feature is in every dataset, by presence, whatever its name). Every other var column of the inputs is kept: as one column when, for every feature, the datasets that have a value for it agree; otherwise per dataset as f"{column}_{handle}" for each dataset that has it. Columns in numeric_var_columns are converted to float; other text columns become categorical (values unchanged).

  • layers, obsm, obsp, uns. Handled by anndata.concat(): a layer or obsm entry present in every dataset is concatenated (obsp block-diagonally), and an uns entry is kept when it is the same in every dataset. varm, varp and raw are not carried into the merged object.

X keeps the common dtype of the inputs (e.g. float32 stays float32).

Parameters:

  • mode (Literal["union", "intersect"]) – How to combine the feature sets (see above).

  • obs_join (Literal["outer", "inner"]) – Which obs columns to keep: of any dataset ("outer") or of every dataset ("inner").

  • obs_columns_to_keep (list[str] | None) – Restrict obs to these joined columns. None keeps all.

  • numeric_var_columns (set[str] | None) – var columns to convert to float.

  • numeric_obs_columns (set[str] | None) – obs columns to convert to float.

  • handle_anndata_key (str) – Name of the obs column that records the dataset of each cell. Defaults to "handle_anndata"; it must not be a column of any dataset.

  • merge (Literal["flag", "sum"]) – See feature_harmonizer().

  • keep_unconverted (bool) – See feature_harmonizer().

Returns:

The merged object; cells in the order of data_h5ad_dict, then of each file.

Return type:

anndata.AnnData

Raises:

ValueError – If mode, obs_join or merge is not one of its values; if a name of obs_columns_to_keep is not among the joined columns, handle_anndata_key is already an obs column, or a numeric column is absent or holds a value that is not a number; if two cells get the same name; if a generated var column name clashes with an input column.

output_plan(table, merge, keep_unconverted)[source]

Decide the output features of one dataset from its feature_table() (a pure function of it).

Rules (also in HarmonizeFeatures):

  • A gene reached by exactly one input feature is one output feature named by the gene ("converted", or "converted_no_final_id" when the gene has no final-database id).

  • A gene reached by several input features (“n-to-1”): with merge="sum" one output feature named by the gene whose values are the sum of theirs ("merged"/"merged_no_final_id"); with merge="flag", if exactly one of them names the gene itself (own) it becomes the gene’s feature and the others stay under their input names as "unconverted_merge_partner"; otherwise all stay under their input names as "unconverted_merge_partner" and the gene has no output feature.

  • Every other input feature stays under its input name ("unconverted_ambiguous", "unconverted_no_conversion", "unconverted_not_in_graph", "unconverted_error") when keep_unconverted, and is left out otherwise; merge partners are always kept.

  • An input name kept unconverted that equals the name of a converted output feature is renamed "unconverted:<name>".

Parameters:

  • table (DataFrame) – Output of feature_table().

  • merge (str) – "sum" or "flag".

  • keep_unconverted (bool) – Keep the unconverted features (see above).

Returns:

One row per output feature, in the order of its first input feature, indexed by the output name, with the columns sources (list of input positions), query_ids (";"-joined input names), status, reason, ensembl_gene, final_id, final_id_alternatives.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

The conversion engine and the graph

class Track(db_manager, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: object

Convert a gene identifier of one Ensembl release into its counterpart at another release.

Track holds the graph (idtrack.TheGraph) and answers one question: given an identifier (an Ensembl gene id with or without version, a transcript or translation id, or an id of an external database such as a gene symbol), optionally the release it comes from, a target release and optionally a target database, which genes correspond to it at the target release, and which ids of the target database those genes carry.

How a conversion works (convert()):

  1. Starting release. With from_release the identifier is read at that release and must be active there. Without it the identifier is read at the target release if it is active there, and at the latest release at which it is active otherwise. The rule is the same for every kind of identifier.

  2. Entry. An identifier that is not a versioned gene id is replaced by the genes it stands for at the starting release: a gene id without version by its version of that release, any other id by the genes that Ensembl’s cross-references of that release attach it to.

  3. History. From those genes the search follows Ensembl’s stable-id history (version changes, merges, splits, retirements) forward or backward in time until the target release. It is a best-first search over states (gene, release): every state is expanded once, so the work is bounded by the size of the part of the history that the query can reach, and every call has a budget.

  4. Bridges. Only when the history leads to no gene at the target release, the search may pass from a gene to another gene that carried the same external id (or the same transcript) at the same time or later (the gap in releases is reported), at most DB.external_search_settings["jump_limit"] times, and it uses as few bridges as possible.

  5. Copies beside the reference sequence. Genes on alternative loci and assembly patches, and LRG records, leave the answer when a gene of the reference sequence was reached too; they are reported apart.

  6. Final conversion. Each gene found is reported as itself or converted to the ids of final_database that are attached to it at the target release.

  7. Order. The result is ordered, best first; prioritize_to_one_filter keeps only the best, which is several genes when the identifier stands for several genes equally (a tie).

Throughout, an edge of the graph counts at a release only on the assembly that was Ensembl’s primary assembly at that release (the primary line of releases): an earlier assembly that Ensembl keeps serving beside a newer one (GRCh37 beside GRCh38) is not part of a conversion.

Results never depend on the order of sets or on the hash seed of the process.

graph

The graph that is queried.

Type:

TheGraph

search_budget_states

Largest number of search states one conversion may expand before SearchBudgetExceededError is raised.

Type:

int

search_budget_seconds

Longest time one conversion may take before the same error is raised.

Type:

float

non_bridging_databases

External databases whose ids are names of a clone or region rather than of a gene; they are never used as a bridge between two genes.

Type:

frozenset[str]

convert(from_id, from_release=None, to_release=None, final_database=None, go_external=True, prioritize_to_one_filter=False, return_path=False, return_ensembl_alternative=True, from_database=None, budget_states=None, budget_seconds=None)[source]

Convert an identifier to the target release and, if asked, to a target database.

Starting release: with from_release the identifier is read at that release and must be active there. Without it, the identifier is read at to_release if it is active there (the answer is then what the identifier means at the target release), and at the latest release at which it is active otherwise. A gene id without version stands for its version of the starting release. The rule is the same for Ensembl ids and for ids of external databases.

Search: from the genes the identifier stands for, Ensembl’s stable-id history is followed to the target release. Only when that leads to no gene, and go_external allows it, the search passes through an external id or transcript that two genes carried at the same time or one after the other, with as few such bridges as possible. external_jump in the result tells how many were used (0: history only).

Final conversion: with final_database each gene found is converted to the ids of that database attached to it at the target release. One result has one final database: genes that have such an id are returned with it; only if none has one, the genes themselves are returned (no_target is then True), or nothing with return_ensembl_alternative=False.

Order: the returned dict is ordered, best first. The genes of the best answer come first, in the order in which prioritize_to_one_filter returns them alone (see “The best answer” below), so the first gene of every answer is the first gene of the best answer. The other genes follow by their evidence: the confidence of the final conversion, the number of bridges, the release gap of the bridges, the support of the query on the entry gene (the number of databases that attach the identifier to that gene at the starting release, to the gene itself or to one of its transcripts or translations), the path score, being the query itself, the number of cross-reference and history steps, and finally the ids themselves.

Copies beside the reference sequence: Ensembl also annotates genes on alternative loci (haplotypes) and assembly patches, and LRG records (LRG_<number>, fixed reference sequences of single genes), each with a stable id of its own and with the names and accessions of the gene it is a copy of. Which genes these are is Ensembl’s statement, kept in the graph (idtrack.TheGraph.is_non_reference() at the target release); nothing is read off an id. When the search reaches genes of the reference sequence and such copies, the copies are not part of the answer, in any strategy; they are listed in alternative_locus_genes. When it reaches copies only (the identifier is such a gene or an LRG record, or a name that only they carry), they are the answer.

Identity: a gene id that exists at the target release is its own answer. The queried gene id’s own version at the target release is never taken out as a copy (a gene that lay on a patch of the assembly of the target release is still that gene), it comes first in the result, and it is the best answer whatever else its history reaches.

The best answer (prioritize_to_one_filter): the queried gene id’s own version at the target release when the search reached it; otherwise the entry genes with the best confidence, bridges, gap and support each contribute their best successor (by score, then being the query itself, then, between successors of the one gene that are still equal, the richest annotation); the mapping score and the annotation are compared among the successors of one entry gene only, because neither says which of two genes an identifier stands for. If more than one gene or target remains (an identifier that several genes carry with equal support, a gene that Ensembl split into equal parts, a gene with several ids in the target database), the answer is a tie: all of them are kept and tie is True. The pairs of a tie are equal in the evidence between entry genes; they are ordered by the mapping score of each to its own entry gene (the higher first), then being the query itself, then the number of steps, then gene id and target id. The assembly cannot differ between candidates, because every candidate lies on the primary assembly of the target release.

Parameters:

  • from_id (str) – The identifier. The graph says which node the string means (idtrack.TheGraph.resolve_name() for from_release, without one for the last release of the graph, and for from_database): a node that exists at that release (as an id of that database, on the assembly that serves the release) before one that does not, whatever the spelling, so a string that is itself the name of a node is not always read as that node. Among those the string is matched exactly before any other way, and “exactly” means as a database wrote the identifier at the release it is read at (the starting release of the rule above), so a name typed as it was written then is that name, not another gene’s synonym spelt the same. A transcript or translation id without version stands for its version of the starting release.

  • from_release (SupportsIndex | None) – The Ensembl release the identifier comes from, an int or another integer type (numpy.int64). None: see above.

  • to_release (SupportsIndex | None) – The target Ensembl release (as from_release). None: the last release of the graph.

  • final_database (str | None) – The database to convert the genes into. None or ensembl_gene: the genes themselves; base_ensembl_gene: gene ids without version; else an external database of the genome assembly of the target release.

  • go_external (bool) – Allow bridges through external ids when the history leads to no gene.

  • prioritize_to_one_filter (bool) – Keep only the best gene and target.

  • return_path (bool) – Include the path to every gene and target in the result.

  • return_ensembl_alternative (bool) – When no gene found has an id in final_database, return the genes themselves instead of nothing.

  • from_database (str | None) – The external database the identifier is meant as. The same string can be an id of several databases (a number that is an NCBI gene id and an id of another source); with this argument the identifier is read as an id of that database: only the genes that this database attaches it to are entered, and an identifier that is not an id of that database (an Ensembl id, an id of other databases only) has no conversion. The database says which genes are meant, not which evidence counts: between the genes entered, the one that more databases attach the identifier to is still the better supported (entry_support). None: all databases.

  • budget_states (int | None) – Largest number of search states this call may expand. None: search_budget_states.

  • budget_seconds (float | None) – Longest time this call may take. None: search_budget_seconds.

Returns:

None when the identifier is unknown or leads to nothing. Otherwise, per gene at the target release (keys in the order described above):

  • from_id (the node the identifier was read as), from_release (the starting release), from_release_inferred, to_release, from_databases (for an external id: the databases through which it was read at the starting release, sorted: every database that attaches it there to one of the genes entered, to the gene itself or to a transcript or translation of the gene; with from_database that database; more than one means the string is an id of several databases there; for an Ensembl id that is not a gene id with version, the Ensembl relation it is read through, e.g. base_ensembl_gene);

  • entry_gene (the gene the identifier was read as at the starting release and from which this gene was reached), entry_support (the number of databases that attach the identifier to it there, to the gene itself or to one of its transcripts or translations; 1 for Ensembl identifiers);

  • external_jump (bridges used), external_gap (releases between leaving a gene and entering the next, summed over the bridges), external_step (cross-reference edges on the path), ensembl_step (history edges on the path);

  • score: the product of Ensembl’s mapping scores along the history edges of the path (1.0 when the path has no scored event);

  • tie: True when the best answer of this conversion is shared by several genes or targets (the same value in every entry of a result);

  • alternative_locus_genes: the genes on alternative loci and patches and the LRG records that the search reached beside genes of the reference sequence, in ascending order; they are not part of the result (the same list in every entry, empty when there is none);

  • the_path (with return_path): a tuple of steps, (source, target, key) for a history edge, (source, target, 0, release) for a cross-reference edge used at a release, and ((None, gene, None),) for a gene that is its own counterpart;

  • final_conversion: final_database, final_conversion_confidence (0: attached at the target release; 1: attached at the target release to a transcript or translation the gene had at another release; None: no gene has an id in the database and the genes themselves are returned), no_target (True in that last case), genes_without_target (the genes the search reached that have no id in the database while other genes have one; they are not part of the result; the same list in every entry), and final_elements: per target id (an id of an external database as that database wrote it at the target release, idtrack.TheGraph.spelling()) a dict with the_path (with return_path) and, with prioritize_to_one_filter, filter_scores.

Return type:

dict | None

Raises:

  • TypeError – If from_id is not a string or a release is not an integer.

  • ValueError – If a release is outside the graph, final_database is not available at the target release, from_database is not an external database of the graph, or a budget is not positive.

  • InactiveAtReleaseError – If from_release is given and the identifier is not active at that release.

  • UnknownVersionError – If the identifier is an Ensembl id with a version that the graph does not hold and that cannot be newer than the graph (an id with a version higher than all the graph holds, active at the graph’s last release, is read as its latest version instead).

  • SearchBudgetExceededError – If the search needs more states or time than the budget of a call.

class TheGraph(*args, backend=None, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: MultiDiGraph

The identifier graph of one organism: Ensembl gene history plus cross-references, with typed accessors.

Nodes are identifiers: versioned Ensembl genes (the backbone, with <id>.Void and <id>.Retired marking births and retirements), versionless base gene ids, transcripts, translations and identifiers of external databases. Two families of edges exist. History edges connect backbone genes and carry the release pair of the event and Ensembl’s mapping score. Cross-reference edges (external id to Ensembl id, base id to versioned gene, transcript to gene, translation to transcript) carry a Connection: the releases in which each database links the two nodes on each assembly.

The class is built by idtrack.GraphMaker and read by idtrack.Track. A graph has two states. While it is being made it is an ordinary networkx.MultiDiGraph. freeze() (called by the first use of any accessor) turns the content into compact arrays: node names and types, edge arrays, and a small table of distinct connections whose release sets are bit masks. A frozen graph cannot be changed, is what save() writes and load() reads back in seconds without network access, and answers every question per node on demand behind bounded caches, so that nothing derived from the graph can be stale and no table over all nodes is kept in memory.

The networkx reading interface (g.nodes[n], g.neighbors(n), g.get_edge_data(u, v), g[u][v][k]) keeps working on a frozen graph; the accessors of this class (history_edges(), xref_edges(), active_ranges(), combined(), resolve_name() …) are the faster way to read it.

Create an empty, mutable graph; arguments are those of networkx.MultiDiGraph.

Parameters:

  • args (Any) – Positional arguments accepted by networkx.MultiDiGraph.__init__().

  • kwargs (Any) – Keyword arguments accepted by networkx.MultiDiGraph.__init__(); they become graph attributes (organism, genome_assembly, ensembl_release, confident_for_release …).

_exists_at(name, release, database)[source]

Tell whether an external identifier exists at a release, and whether it is an id of a database at all.

An identifier exists at a release where one of its links holds on the assembly that serves the release (served_mask()), as the engine reads a link and as the spelling of a release is chosen. What an assembly lists at a release it does not serve does not make an identifier exist there: human GRCh37 lists its names of release 75 at every later release, and a name that GRCh38 gave up long ago does not exist today. An identifier that only such an assembly ever has exists at no release in this sense; it is still found, as an identifier that exists elsewhere (resolve_name()).

Parameters:

  • release (int) – The release.

  • database (str | None) – The database the identifier must be an id of; None: any.

Returns:

Whether the node exists at the release (as an id of database when one is named), and whether it is an id of database at any release (True without a database).

Return type:

tuple[bool, bool]

active_ranges(node)[source]

Return the release ranges in which a node exists: [[first, last], ...], inclusive and ascending.

For a backbone gene the ranges come from its history edges: a range starts at the new_release of an edge that enters the node and ends at the old_release of the last edge that leaves it; the last range of an id that is alive at the last release of the graph ends at infinity. For every other node the ranges are the releases of its cross-reference edges, whatever the database and assembly.

property hyperconnective_nodes: dict[str, int]

External identifiers that more genes share at one time than an identity can, with that number of genes.

An external id is hyper-connective when, in a single Ensembl release, it is linked to more than genes_at_once_threshold different genes (genes_linked_at_once(): genes by stable id, whatever their versions; a transcript or a translation counts as its gene). Such ids are names of gene families and accessions shared by paralogues (RFAM families, U6, 5S_rRNA, snoRNA names): they say what kind of gene something is, not which gene. Following them in a synonym search multiplies the candidates and bridges unrelated genes, so the search does not follow them.

The count is per release, so the set does not grow with the number of releases in the graph: an id linked to many successive versions of one gene, or to a few genes that change over the years, is not hyper-connective, however many edges it has. The threshold was chosen by measurement against Ensembl’s own data (pig: with 5, no kind of query is answered worse and 15 kinds better than with the earlier rule, more than 20 edges over all releases; with 10 or 20 the family ids shared by 6 to 20 genes become bridges and conversions of retired ids get worse). It is read when this property is read, so it can be changed on the class without building a graph again.

Returns:

{external node: largest number of genes linked in one release} for the hyper-connective nodes.

Return type:

dict[str, int]

resolve_name(identifier, release=None, database=None, target=None)[source]

Find the node a user’s string means at a release, and say how it was matched.

This is the one place that says what a typed string means; the engine, the API, the inference of the source of a list and the self-tests all ask it, each naming the release it means.

Two things decide, in this order:

Existence at the release the question is about. Between the nodes the string can mean, one that exists at release (without one: at the last release of the graph) is taken before one that does not. Databases reuse strings: slit2 was a synonym of one gene years ago and is, in another letter case, the name of another gene today; APC10 was the name of one gene and is a synonym of another today. Which of the two is meant depends on the release asked about, not on how the string happens to be spelt. An Ensembl stable id (of a gene, with or without version, a transcript or a translation) is never passed over for an external identifier or synonym spelt the same, at whatever release it exists: it is an id of Ensembl’s own history, which the graph follows through the releases. An external identifier exists at a release where a database has it on the genome assembly that serves the release (serving_line), as the engine counts a link: what an earlier assembly that Ensembl keeps listing beside the primary one says at such a release (human GRCh37, with its names of release 75 at every later release) does not make an identifier exist there, so a name that GRCh38 gave up and that is a synonym of a gene today is that synonym today. An identifier that only such an assembly ever has exists at no release and is still found (below). When the caller says which external database the string is an id of (database), “exists” means “is an id of that database at the release”, and among the nodes that are not, one that is an id of that database at some release comes before one that never is.

The steps, among the nodes that are equal in existence. They are tried in this order, each only if the one before found nothing. Each of the first four is tried on the names of the graph and then on its synonyms (the synonym node of the string, synonym_id::<string>; the match is then reported as "synonym:<step>") before the next step begins, so that a string that is exactly a synonym of one gene is that synonym, not a spelling variant of another gene’s name (H3.3B, a synonym, is not the name H3-3b):

  1. "exact": the string is an identifier exactly as it is written. For an Ensembl id that is the name of its node. For an external identifier it is how a database (the one named, when database is given) writes it at the release the identifier is read at: release when the identifier exists there; without release the release a conversion reads it at, which is target when the identifier exists there and its latest release otherwise (the same when release does not hold it). Databases change the letter case of a name over the releases, and two databases may write one name in two ways at one release; the graph keeps one node per identifier, named as at its last release, and how each database wrote it at each release (spelling()). So PRR2, typed for a release at which a database wrote the name so, is that name exactly, although the node is called prr2 after today’s spelling, and it is not taken for another gene’s synonym PRR2; typed prr2 for that release it is the same name by letter case.

  2. "case": it is a node name when letter case is ignored.

  3. "separator": it is a node name when -, _ and . are taken as the same character (and case is ignored): HLA_A and HLA.A for HLA-A, ENSG00000123456_2 for ENSG00000123456.2.

  4. "version": the string ends in .<digits> and the identifier without that suffix is an id of a database of sequence accessions (idtrack.DB.accession_database_prefixes: RefSeq, UniProt, CCDS and the like) and of no symbol database of the organism (idtrack.DB.symbol_databases): NM_000546.9 for NM_000546. Nothing else is ever cut off the name of an external identifier: SLA.7 and SLA_11 are not SLA, NM_713028147 is not NM.

  5. "version_newer_than_graph": the string is an Ensembl id with a version higher than every version the graph holds of it (written with ., _ or -), and the id is active at the last release of the graph: the version may belong to a release newer than the graph, so the string stands for the latest version the graph holds, ENSG00000123456.99 for ENSG00000123456.7. Any other version that the graph does not hold (a lower one, one in a gap, any version of a retired id) matches nothing; known_versions() then names the versions that exist.

When no node the string can mean exists at the release, the first one in the order of the steps is returned (with database: the first that is an id of that database at all, else the first), and the caller learns from the node where it does exist. The cost is a few dictionary look-ups, whatever the string.

Parameters:

  • identifier (str) – The string to resolve.

  • release (SupportsIndex | None) – The Ensembl release the question is about (for a conversion: the release the identifier is read at, from_release). None means the last release of the graph. A release the graph does not have is one at which no external identifier exists.

  • database (str | None) – The external database the string is meant as an id of (for a conversion: from_database). None: any database.

  • target (SupportsIndex | None) – Only without release: the release a conversion goes to (to_release), at which an identifier is read when it exists there. It says at which release the spelling of an identifier is judged in the step "exact"; which node exists is asked at the last release of the graph all the same. None: the last release of the graph.

Returns:

The node name and how it was matched, or (None, None).

Return type:

tuple[str | None, str | None]

Raises:

TypeError – If identifier is not a string, or release or target is not an integer.

The view shares the arrays and the per-node caches of the graph; rev.neighbors(n) are the predecessors of n. The typed accessors of the view (history_edges(), xref_edges()) are reversed as well; everything that describes a node (active_ranges(), combined() …) is that of the graph itself.

TheGraph

Write the graph to a file, atomically.

The file is a NumPy .npz archive (no pickled objects): the node names, node types, edge arrays, the table of distinct connections with their release bit masks, the genes outside the reference sequence with their releases, the name indices, and one JSON document with the graph attributes, the manifest and the graph-wide tables. It is written to a temporary file in the same folder and renamed, so an interrupted run leaves either the previous file or none, never a part of one.

class GraphMaker(db_manager)[source]

Bases: object

Builds the identifier graph of one organism and keeps it in the local repository.

The graph (idtrack.TheGraph) holds the history of Ensembl gene ids over the releases of the manager’s window, the transcripts and translations of every release linked to their genes, versionless base gene ids, and the identifiers of the selected external databases linked to the Ensembl ids they annotate.

The history is not copied from Ensembl’s mapping_session table unchecked: the releases of every event are validated against the id tables of the releases (which ids exist where), sessions whose recorded releases contradict the tables are corrected, and every correction is logged and recorded in the graph’s manifest.

A built graph is written as one file whose manifest says what it was built from; get_graph() loads a file only if that manifest is what is asked for.

Class initialization.

Parameters:

db_manager (DatabaseManager) – Needed to download all necessary tables and data frames. It contains the temporary directory to save the resultant graph.

Raises:

ValueError – If the release of db_manager is not the newest release of its window. A graph is the snapshot of the releases ignore_before to ignore_after; it is built from the newest of them.

_check_history_reaches_back(db_manager, releases, old_releases)[source]

Stop if the id-history table starts later than Ensembl’s history does within the window of the graph.

The id-history table is kept in the local repository and is computed for a release window. A table that was computed for a later window lacks the early sessions, and a graph built from it silently has no history there. Ensembl’s mapping_session table of the snapshot release lists all sessions; when it has sessions in the window before the first one of the id-history table, the events of those sessions are counted in Ensembl’s stable_id_event table, and events of this form there mean that the stored table is not the table of this window.

Parameters:

_merge_spellings(names, types, edges, backbone_assembly)[source]

Choose one node for the external identifiers that are equal in lower case, and keep how each is written.

A release belongs to the assembly that serves it in the backbone (backbone_assembly). What another assembly says at that release does not count while a serving assembly says anything: human GRCh37 is frozen and still listed at every release that GRCh38 serves, with the spellings of the time it was frozen. Only an identifier (or a database of it) that no serving assembly has at any release is judged by all its assemblies.

The node keeps the spelling that Ensembl gives at the latest release in which the identifier exists. Where several spellings exist at that release, the one carried by more (database, Ensembl id) links at that release wins, then the one with more upper-case letters, then the first in sort order.

For every database of the identifier the spelling of each release is kept as well (the same rule within the database: more links of the database at the release, more upper-case letters, sort order), so that a conversion to a release returns the identifier as the database wrote it at that release (idtrack.TheGraph.spelling()).

Parameters:

  • names (list[str]) – Node names by provisional number.

  • types (list[str]) – Node types by provisional number.

  • edges (dict[tuple[str, int], dict[int, int]]) – The cross-reference edges collected so far.

  • backbone_assembly (dict[int, int]) – The assembly that serves each release of the graph.

Returns:

{number of a merged spelling: number of the node that stays} and, only for the databases that write the identifier otherwise than the node is named at some release, {(number of the node that stays, database): (spelling of the database at its latest release, ((release mask, spelling), ...))}; the pairs name the releases at which the database wrote it otherwise than at its latest release.

Raises:

ValueError – If a name that differs only in case from another one is not an external identifier.

Return type:

tuple[dict[int, int], dict[tuple[int, str], tuple[str, tuple[tuple[int, str], …]]]]

construct_graph(narrow=True, form_list=None, narrow_external=True)[source]

Build the graph from the tables of the manager.

The steps: the gene history (history()), the transcripts and translations of every release, the genes that lie outside the reference sequence (_non_reference_genes()), the relations between the forms, the identifiers of the external databases, the Ensembl ids that exist on another assembly only, and the versionless base gene ids. External identifiers that differ only in letter case are one node, named with the spelling that Ensembl gives at the latest release in which the identifier exists; how each database wrote it at each release is kept beside it (_merge_spellings(), idtrack.TheGraph.spelling()).

Parameters:

  • narrow (bool) – If False, the manifest of the graph also lists Ensembl’s mapping sessions with their database names, assemblies and dates (read from the full id-history table). The graph itself is the same.

  • form_list (list | None) – The forms to include, a list of ‘gene’, ‘transcript’, ‘translation’ that contains ‘gene’. If None, all forms of the manager.

  • narrow_external (bool) – If False, every external database of Ensembl is included, not only those selected in the organism’s externals YAML file. The graph becomes much larger and conversions slower.

Returns:

The frozen graph, with its manifest in graph.graph["manifest"].

Raises:

  • ValueError – If the Ensembl ids of the organism carry no versions in some release (such organisms are not supported; raised by the manager when the ids are read, before anything else is done), or if the tables contradict each other (an edge to a node that does not exist, an external table that names an Ensembl id which the primary assembly does not have).

history(db_manager, narrow=True)[source]

Build the history edges of one form from the id tables of the releases and Ensembl’s id-history table.

The id tables say which <id>.<version> exists in which release (each release from the assembly that serves it in the backbone). From them come the edges of an id with itself: <id>.Void → <id>.<v> at its first appearance, <id>.<v> → <id>.<w> at a change of version, <id>.<v> → <id>.Retired when it disappears, <id>.Retired → <id>.<v> when it comes back, and a self-loop to infinity on every id of the last release.

Ensembl’s stable_id_event table says which id passed into which other id (and which id was re-mapped onto itself with a score below 1, or onto itself in a session that also maps it to or from another id), per mapping session. The releases of a session are not taken from mapping_session: an event from A to B belongs to the pair of consecutive releases at which A exists in the first and B in the second. For every session the pair that most of its events fit is determined; it replaces the recorded pair where the two differ (Ensembl’s pig session 106 to 107 is recorded as 106 to 104; sessions over a gap such as rhesus 50 to 52 belong to 51 to 52). An event that does not fit its session’s pair is placed at the nearest pair it fits; an event that fits no pair, or whose ids are in no id table, contradicts the tables and is left out. All of it is counted in the report.

Parameters:

  • db_manager (DatabaseManager) – The manager of the form, at the snapshot release.

  • narrow (bool) – Read the narrow id-history table (True) or the full one, whose session metadata then goes into the report.

Returns:

The edges as (source, target, old_release, new_release, weight, key) tuples (new_release is infinity on the self-loops of the last release), sorted, and the report for the manifest: the sessions with recorded and used release pairs and their counts, and the corrections.

Raises:

  • HistoryValidationError – If the events of a session fit no pair of consecutive releases, fit several pairs equally well without the recorded one among them, or if the id-history table does not reach back to the first release of the graph although Ensembl’s mapping_session does (a table computed for another release window).

  • ValueError – If an id of the last release is missing from the backbone, or if the ids of a release carry no versions (raised by the manager, see construct_graph()).

Return type:

tuple[list[tuple], dict[str, Any]]

class ReleaseSet[source]

An immutable set of Ensembl releases with its bit mask, one object per distinct value.

It is a frozenset (membership, iteration, |, &, min, max and comparison with any set work as usual) that also carries mask, an int whose bit r is set when release r is in the set, so that mask >> r & 1 tests membership and |/& on masks combine sets without building them. Equal sets are the same object: a graph with millions of edges holds a few thousand of them.

served_mask(items, line, database=None, exclude=frozenset({}))[source]

Return the releases at which a cross-reference link holds, each counted on the assembly that serves it.

This is the one rule for where a link counts. The builder chooses the spelling of a release by it, the engine follows a link by it, and the name resolution says by it whether an identifier exists at a release: a link that an assembly lists at a release it does not serve (serving_line()) is not a link of that release.

  • exclude (frozenset) – Databases that do not count.

Returns:

The bit mask of the releases (bit r set: the link holds at release r).

Return type:

int

serving_line(backbone_assembly)[source]

Return, per genome assembly, the releases that the assembly serves in the backbone.

A release belongs to one assembly: the one that serves it in the backbone of the graph (TheGraph.backbone_assembly). An earlier assembly that Ensembl keeps listing beside the primary one (human GRCh37, frozen with its annotation of release 75 and listed at every later release) serves none of the releases that the primary assembly has.

class DB[source]

Bases: object

Store constants shared across IDTrack modules for Ensembl data access and graph construction.

This class centralizes every constant that multiple components (e.g. idtrack.GraphMaker, idtrack.Track) rely on when talking to the Ensembl FTP mirror, REST API, and public MySQL instances. Housing the values in one namespace prevents circular imports, ensures a single source of truth, and simplifies testing. DB is never instantiated; import the class and reference its attributes directly. The organism table is the only part meant to change at run time, and only through DB.register_organism().

The derived dictionaries and sets are updated in place, and register_organism() changes the table and symbol_databases in place too, so references to any of them taken earlier stay current. classmethod _validate_organism_table(table, symbol_databases, organism_aliases=None)[source]

Check the organism table and the symbol-database table for consistency.

Rules: organism names are lower-case Ensembl production names; every organism has at least one assembly; assembly keys are positive integers; each entry carries Ports (known MySQL ports, see mysql_port_min_release, and none that mysql_port_assembly reserves for another assembly), Priority and ReleaseRange, plus optionally Name and DbSuffix and nothing else; priorities are unique per organism and start at 1; release ranges are [first, last] with last None or not smaller than first; entries of one organism that share a DbSuffix have non-overlapping release ranges; the symbol-database table names exactly the organisms of the organism table; aliases belong to organisms of the table, are lower-case words that are no organism name, and no alias is declared for two organisms.

Parameters:

  • table (Mapping[str, Mapping[int, Mapping[str, Any]]]) – Candidate value of assembly_mysqlport_priority.

  • symbol_databases (Mapping[str, Sequence[str]]) – Candidate value of symbol_databases.

  • organism_aliases (Mapping[str, Sequence[str]] | None) – Candidate value of organism_aliases; None for a table without aliases.

Raises:

ValueError – If any rule is violated; the message names the organism, the assembly and the rule.

Return type:

None

classmethod register_organism(name, assemblies, symbol_databases=None, aliases=None)[source]

Add an organism to the organism table, or replace its entry, and recompute the derived attributes.

This is the supported way to try an organism that idtrack does not declare (or to change a declared one) within a Python session; to make it permanent, add the same entry to assembly_mysqlport_priority in idtrack/_db.py. The whole table is validated before anything changes (see _validate_organism_table()), so a rejected entry leaves the table as it was. The table, symbol_databases and the derived attributes are updated in place, so references to them taken earlier stay current.

Example

>>> DB.register_organism(
...     "danio_rerio",
...     {11: {"Name": "GRCz11", "Ports": [3306, 5306], "Priority": 1, "ReleaseRange": [92, None]}},
...     symbol_databases=["ZFIN"],
... )
Parameters:

  • name (str) – Ensembl production name of the organism (e.g. "danio_rerio").

  • assemblies (Mapping[int, Mapping[str, Any]]) – {assembly key: entry} with the fields described in the comment block of assembly_mysqlport_priority.

  • symbol_databases (Sequence[str] | None) – Ordered gene-symbol databases of the organism (names as in its externals YAML). Required for a new organism (an empty list if it has none, in which case idtrack.HarmonizeFeatures needs an explicit final_database). When an organism already in the table is replaced and this is omitted (None), its current symbol databases are kept.

  • aliases (Sequence[str] | None) – Short names of the organism (lower case, e.g. ["zebrafish"]), which then resolve to it wherever an organism is asked for. None keeps the aliases of an organism that is replaced and gives a new organism none.

Raises:

ValueError – If symbol_databases is omitted for a new organism, or if the resulting table violates a rule of _validate_organism_table().

Return type:

None

class DatabaseManager(organism, form, local_repository, ensembl_release=None, ignore_before=None, ignore_after=None, store_raw_always=True, genome_assembly=None)[source]

Bases: object

Manage retrieval, preprocessing, and storage of Ensembl Core and related external datasets.

The DatabaseManager centralizes all low-level operations required for ID-track analyses, including discovering which Ensembl releases are available for a given organism/assembly, downloading the corresponding MySQL tables, normalizing column names, persisting raw and processed files under a local cache directory, and orchestrating auxiliary look-ups to third-party resources via ExternalDatabases. By funnelling every data-access path through a single object the wider package gains:

  • Stable, reproducible builds - every graph, lookup table, or ID-history file is anchored to the exact Ensembl release, genome assembly, and form (gene, transcript, translation, …) with which the manager was configured.

  • Transparent caching - expensive downloads happen once; every table is kept in a file of its own in the local repository (tables_directory), written atomically and named by everything it depends on (release, form, externals selection), so a table computed for other parameters is never served.

  • Versioned ids only - idtrack follows <id>.<version> through the releases. A release whose Ensembl ids carry no versions (some organisms, e.g. S. cerevisiae) is refused where its id table is read (create_ids()), with an error that says so: no table is made up for it.

Key public methods/attributes

  • available_releases() — list releases of the assembly within the ignore window.

  • change_release() — a new manager for another Ensembl release (likewise change_form(), change_assembly(), change_release_auto_assembly()).

  • get_table() — a raw Ensembl table (stored after the first download); download_table() fetches one without storing it.

  • get_db() — a derived table (ids, history, relations, cross references).

  • create_external_all() — the cross references of every assembly the externals YAML enables for the release.

  • organism, form, ensembl_release, genome_assembly — core configuration knobs, surfaced for quick inspection.

A manager’s configuration does not change after construction; the change_* methods return new managers. Use the built-in __str__() for a concise, human-readable dump of that state.

Initialize a DatabaseManager for a specific organism, release, and assembly.

param organism:

Canonical species name in Ensembl schema (e.g. "homo_sapiens"); one of idtrack.DB.supported_organisms, otherwise NotImplementedError is raised.

type organism:

str

param form:

Biological entity level of interest—one of "gene", "transcript", "translation", …—governing which stable-ID columns will be expected downstream.

type form:

str

param local_repository:

Directory of the cached tables (tables_directory, one HDF5 file per table), the saved index of Ensembl’s dumps and the graphs. It must exist and be readable; it must be writable only when a table has to be computed and stored (a read-only repository serves what it holds).

type local_repository:

str

param ensembl_release:

Target Ensembl release number. If None the most recent release available for genome_assembly is selected automatically.

type ensembl_release:

Optional[int]

param ignore_before:

Earliest release to include when building cross-release ID histories. Defaults to the first release of the organism in the organism table (idtrack.DB.first_release(), over all its assemblies), the same default as idtrack.API uses.

type ignore_before:

Optional[int]

param ignore_after:

Latest release to include when building histories. np.inf (the default) disables the upper bound and includes all newer releases.

type ignore_after:

Optional[int | float]

param store_raw_always:

When True (default) raw Ensembl tables are stored in the repository after their download; when False they are not, and every derived table that needs them downloads them again.

type store_raw_always:

bool

param genome_assembly:

Assembly key of the organism table (idtrack.DB.assembly_mysqlport_priority), as an integer of any integer type, an integral float or a string of digits (idtrack.DB.assembly_key()). This selects the primary assembly used for data access (e.g. 38 = human GRCh38, 39 = mouse GRCm39, 111 = pig Sscrofa11.1, 10 = rhesus Mmul_10). The key usually equals the code in core schema names (<organism>_core_<release>_<code>); see the table’s DbSuffix. If omitted, the highest-priority assembly for organism is used. If ensembl_release is provided, the selection is restricted to assemblies that actually contain that release; otherwise to assemblies with a release inside the ignore_before/ignore_after window.

type genome_assembly:

Optional[int]

raises ValueError:

If form is not in the supported list, local_repository fails basic path/read/write checks, or the Ensembl access mode (IDTRACK_ENSEMBL_ACCESS / idtrack.DB.ensembl_access) is invalid.

raises RuntimeError:

If internal port/release configuration is inconsistent.

raises NotImplementedError:

If organism is not in the organism table (idtrack.DB.supported_organisms).

_create_relation_helper(df)[source]

Convert an ID/version matrix into the canonical three-column relationship table.

The helper is used by DatabaseManager.create_relation_current() and is not intended for direct use. It validates the incoming frame, keeps the versions of genes and transcripts as integers and those of translations as NaN-compatible floats (a transcript without translation has none), casts all stable-ID columns to string, and finally compresses each ID + version pair into the compact node label used throughout ID-track graphs.

Parameters:

df (pandas.DataFrame) – A six-column frame with exactly the following names (order irrelevant): gene_stable_id, gene_version, transcript_stable_id, transcript_version, translation_stable_id, translation_version.

Returns:

Three columns—gene, transcript,

translation—deduplicated and index-reset, ready for graph construction.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

ValueError – If df does not contain the required six columns or if version columns cannot be coerced to the expected numeric dtype.

static _determine_usecols_ids(form)[source]

Determine column subsets needed to fetch identifier tables for a given Ensembl molecular form.

The helper translates a user-facing form string ("gene", "transcript", or "translation") into three ordered lists that drive low-level SQL selects throughout ID-track. Splitting the information this way lets public routines such as DatabaseManager.create_ids() assemble the minimal column set required for each organism/release while still keeping associated keys available for later joins.

Parameters:

form (str) – Molecular form whose identifier columns are requested. Must be one of idtrack.DB.forms_in_order ("gene", "transcript", or "translation").

  • usecols_asso - foreign-key columns linking form to upstream forms, enabling later joins (e.g., ["transcript_id", "gene_id"] for transcripts).

Return type:

tuple[list[str], list[str], list[str]]

ValueError – If form is not in {"gene", "transcript", "translation"}.
