classmethod _get_core_db_index(*, organism, genome_assembly, local_repository=None, needed_up_to=None)[source]

Return cached core-DB availability for an (organism, assembly) pair across all configured ports.

The Ensembl public MySQL service can host the same assembly on multiple ports depending on release (e.g. homo_sapiens assembly 37). To support full-history workflows we build a small in-memory index:

  • ports: ports probed for this (organism, assembly) in preference order

  • releases_by_port: releases available for this assembly on each reachable port

  • db_by_port_release: schema name for each available release on each reachable port

  • releases: sorted union of all releases across ports

  • port_for_release: deterministic choice of port for each release (first configured port that has it)

  • db_for_release: chosen schema name for each release (matching port_for_release, includes patch-letter suffixes)

Both sources (the MySQL probe and the HTTPS scan) look for core databases named with the assembly’s DbSuffix and accept only releases inside its ReleaseRange (see _release_window()), so they return the same releases for an assembly. The index is cached per process and per version of the organism table. The HTTPS part is also saved in local_repository (see _https_index()) and read from there when it covers the releases up to needed_up_to, so that no Ensembl REST call and no dump scan is needed for a window that ends at a release the saved scan already reached.

Parameters:

  • organism (str) – Canonical Ensembl organism name (e.g. "homo_sapiens").

  • genome_assembly (int) – Assembly key of the organism table (e.g. 38 for GRCh38).

  • local_repository (str | None) – Folder of the caller’s cached tables, where the HTTPS index is saved; None keeps it in memory only.

  • needed_up_to (int | None) – Last release the caller needs (its ignore_after); None means the latest Ensembl release.

Returns:

Mapping describing reachable releases/ports for this organism/assembly.

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

If the dump scan cannot be completed (a request stays unanswered), its idtrack.EnsemblDownloadError propagates; no partial index is ever returned or cached. An unknown organism or assembly raises the organism table’s error.

classmethod _get_core_db_index_from_ftp(*, organism, genome_assembly, ports)[source]

Build a core-DB availability index by probing the Ensembl HTTPS/FTP MySQL dumps.

Every release of the assembly’s window (_release_window(), up to Ensembl’s latest release) is looked up with _ftp_find_core_db_dir(). A release is left out only when Ensembl answered that it has no core database of this assembly; a request that fails after its retries raises, so an incomplete index is never built (and never cached or saved). An assembly that has no release at all gives an index with an empty release list. A request that stays unanswered raises idtrack.EnsemblDownloadError; if the latest Ensembl release cannot be learnt, idtrack.EnsemblRestError propagates.

Parameters:

  • organism (str) – Ensembl species name.

  • genome_assembly (int) – Assembly key of the organism table.

  • ports (list[int]) – Configured MySQL ports of the assembly (releases are assigned to them).

Returns:

The index (see _get_core_db_index()), with scanned_up_to.

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

classmethod _https_index(*, organism, genome_assembly, ports, local_repository, needed_up_to)[source]

Return the HTTPS-dump index, from local_repository when a saved one covers the need, else scanned.

The scan asks Ensembl REST for the latest release and probes the dump directory of every release, so a saved index is what lets a manager whose window ends at a known release (every graph built or loaded through idtrack.API.build_graph()) work without the network once its tables and graph are on disk.

Parameters:

  • organism (str) – Ensembl species name.

  • genome_assembly (int) – Assembly key of the organism table.

  • ports (list[int]) – Configured MySQL ports of the assembly.

  • local_repository (str | None) – Folder where the index is saved; None neither reads nor saves one.

  • needed_up_to (int | None) – Last release needed; None for the latest Ensembl release.

Returns:

The HTTPS-dump index; scanned_live_at (time.monotonic()) is set when it was scanned in this call.

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

_require_versions(df, version_column, form)[source]

Return df with the versions of its ids as integers; refuse ids that carry no version.

idtrack follows <id>.<version> through the releases: the graph’s nodes, the history and the tables that feed them are named that way. Ensembl gives the ids of some organisms no versions (S. cerevisiae: YAL001C), in all or in some releases. Such an organism is not supported, and nothing is made up for it (no synthetic version, no table without versions): the id table of the release is refused here, and with it every table that is derived from it.

pandas.DataFrame

The set is discovered via available_releases_versions(), filtered against ignore_before / ignore_after, sorted in ascending order, and cached for the lifetime of this DatabaseManager instance. The resulting list represents releases that can safely be queried and cached locally, guaranteeing reproducible downstream analyses.

Return all Ensembl releases that have a core database of at least one configured assembly.

For clean-handoff species (e.g. mouse: 37 → 38 → 39), no single assembly spans the full release history. Graph construction and YAML template generation therefore need a release catalogue that is the union over all assemblies configured for organism in idtrack.DB.assembly_mysqlport_priority.

The list is filtered by the manager’s ignore_before / ignore_after window and cached for the lifetime of this DatabaseManager instance. Every assembly’s index must be complete: if one cannot be built (Ensembl does not answer), the error is raised instead of leaving that assembly’s releases out.

List the core databases of the organism’s configured assemblies, each within its release range.

The names come from the core-database index of every assembly in the organism table (_get_core_db_index()): databases named with the assembly’s DbSuffix (patch letters included, e.g. homo_sapiens_core_54_36p) whose release lies in the assembly’s ReleaseRange and at or above release 48. The index merges the live MySQL catalogue (where its ports are usable) with the HTTPS dump listings, so the list is the same whichever way Ensembl is reached. The resulting frames are concatenated, enriched with assembly, release, form, and organism columns, and returned to the caller. When just_download is True the downloads are still performed (ensuring they are cached on disk for future runs) but an empty dataframe is returned to avoid unnecessary memory use.

pandas.DataFrame

create_external_all(return_mode, narrow_external=True)[source]

Download and collate cross-reference mappings from every supported genome assembly.

The manager cycles through every genome assembly recognised for the current organism (ordered by idtrack.DB.assembly_mysqlport_priority), fetches either the filtered external_relevant mapping table (when narrow_external=True) or the full external mapping table (when narrow_external=False) for each via get_db(), labels every row with its source assembly, and finally concatenates the tables. Because this helper is intended for ad-hoc inspection only, it bypasses the get_db() caching layer and therefore never writes the result to the local repository.

Parameters:

  • return_mode (str) – Strategy for handling rows that appear in more than one assembly.

  • narrow_external (bool) –

    If True (default), restrict results to databases enabled in the external YAML configuration (external_relevant). If False, include all external databases provided by the Ensembl MySQL server (external).

    • "all"

      Keep one copy of every unique (release, graph_id, id_db, name_db, ensembl_identity, xref_identity, assembly) combination. Duplicates are resolved within each assembly only.

    • "unique"

      Keep one copy of every unique (release, graph_id, id_db, name_db, ensembl_identity, xref_identity) combination across all assemblies, preferring the assembly with the highest priority. (Currently no downstream use case.)

    • "duplicated"

      Return only the rows that occur in more than one assembly as a pandas.core.groupby.generic.DataFrameGroupBy, keyed by the same column set used for "unique". (Currently no downstream use case.)

Returns:

  • If return_mode is "all" or "unique",

    a de-duplicated cross-reference table with the columns release, graph_id, id_db, name_db, ensembl_identity, xref_identity, and assembly.

  • If return_mode is "duplicated",

    a group-by view containing only duplicated entries.

Return type:

Union[pandas.DataFrame, pandas.core.groupby.generic.DataFrameGroupBy]

Raises:

ValueError – If return_mode is not "all", "unique", or "duplicated".

create_external_db(filter_mode)[source]

Retrieve Ensembl-external-ID relationships and/or database statistics.

This consolidates a complex SQL join—spanning Ensembl core tables gene, transcript, translation and the cross-reference tables xref, object_xref, identity_xref, external_db, and external_synonym—into a single pandas dataframe. It enables downstream analyses such as mapping Ensembl gene models to UniProt, RefSeq, or CCDS identifiers, or summarising which external sources are represented in a given Ensembl release. The result type and granularity are controlled by filter_mode, allowing either the raw relationship rows or a per-database count to be returned.

The query executed is conceptually equivalent to the (simplified) MySQL statement below, though the actual SQL is constructed programmatically for flexibility and performance:

SELECT g.stable_id, t.stable_id, tr.stable_id, x.dbprimary_acc, edb.db_name, es.synonym, ix.*
FROM gene g
JOIN transcript t USING (gene_id)
JOIN translation tr USING (transcript_id)
JOIN object_xref ox ON (g.gene_id = ox.ensembl_id AND ox.ensembl_object_type = "Gene")
JOIN xref x ON (ox.xref_id = x.xref_id)
LEFT JOIN external_db edb ON (x.external_db_id = edb.external_db_id)
LEFT JOIN identity_xref ix ON (ox.object_xref_id = ix.object_xref_id)
LEFT JOIN external_synonym es ON (x.xref_id = es.xref_id)
LIMIT 10;

When tighter genomic scoping is required the gene table can be prefixed with coord_system and seq_region:

FROM coord_system cs
JOIN seq_region  sr USING (coord_system_id)
JOIN gene        g  USING (seq_region_id)

You can experiment interactively against the public Ensembl MySQL mirror:

mysql --user=anonymous --host=ensembldb.ensembl.org -D homo_sapiens_core_105_38 -A
# Schema reference:
# https://m.ensembl.org/info/docs/api/core/core_schema.html
Parameters:

filter_mode (str) –

Controls both the row subset and the output schema. Must be one of:

  • "all" - return every mapping found in MySQL, no post-filtering applied.

  • "relevant" - return only mappings whose external database is marked Include: true in the

    ExternalDatabases.give_list_for_case() YAML configuration.

  • "database" - return a two-column summary (name_db, count) for all external databases.

  • "relevant-database" - as above, but restricted to databases flagged Include: true.

    The special values "relevant" and "relevant-database" implicitly consult the cached external_inst to honour the user’s curated allow-list.

Returns:

  • For "all" / "relevant" - six-column frame

    ["release", "graph_id", "id_db", "name_db", "ensembl_identity", "xref_identity"] holding one row per Ensembl→external identifier edge. graph_id is the Ensembl stable ID (+version), while the two identity columns store Smith-Waterman percent identities (float16) for QC.

  • For "database" / "relevant-database" - two-column frame

    ["name_db", "count"] giving the number of rows of each external database (most rows first, ties by name). count is an int64.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

  • ValueError – If filter_mode is not one of the accepted literals or if the YAML allow-list claims a database that is absent from the retrieved mappings—indicating the configuration and MySQL data are out of sync.

  • EnsemblSchemaError – If identity_xref lacks columns other than its identity columns.

Notes

Synonym handling - any synonym brought in from external_synonym is prefixed with DB.synonym_id_nodes_prefix, and its name_db is likewise prefixed so that synonym nodes remain distinguishable during graph building. Caching - this method always computes; get_db() stores and reuses its results (external, external_database, and external_relevant keyed by the enabled databases). The raw tables it reads are stored by get_table(). Restriction first - with relevant the raw tables are restricted to the enabled databases before the join (identical result, a fraction of the memory). External ids and synonyms are stripped of surrounding white space; ids that are empty after it are dropped. The rows are in a total order (database, Ensembl id, external id, identities).

create_gene_region()[source]

Tell for every gene of the release whether it lies on the reference sequence of the assembly.

Ensembl annotates genes on the chromosomes and scaffolds of an assembly (its reference sequence) and also on sequence regions beside it: alternative loci (haplotypes), assembly patches and LRG records. A gene on such a region is a copy of, or an alternative to, a gene of the reference sequence and has a stable id of its own. The core database marks these regions with the attribute idtrack.DB.non_reference_attribute (seq_region_attrib joined to attrib_type), in every release and for every kind of region; the table assembly_exception lists only some of them and is empty in recent human releases, so it is not read.

The table is a function of three raw tables of the release (gene with its sequence region, seq_region_attrib and attrib_type) and of the gene ids (idsraw_gene).

Returns:

One row per gene of the release: gene_stable_id, gene_version (as in the ids table of the gene form) and non_reference (True for a gene on a region outside the reference sequence). A release whose core database defines no such attribute or marks no region has False throughout.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

ValueError – If a gene of the id table has no sequence region in the gene table.

create_id_history(narrow)[source]

Retrieve historical relationships between successive Ensembl stable IDs.

Build a cross-release lineage table mapping every obsolete ID version to its immediate successor for the configured organism and form, over every mapping session that the release’s tables record (all earlier releases; get_db() restricts it to the manager’s window). The information is assembled from the Core tables stable_id_event and mapping_session and then normalised so that all identifiers follow the canonical <stable_id>.<version> convention. Downstream graph-construction utilities depend on this table to reconstruct how genes, transcripts, or translations evolve across Ensembl releases.

Parameters:

narrow (bool) – If True drop auxiliary columns (mapping session metadata, assembly labels, creation timestamps, etc.) to minimise on-disk footprint; otherwise return the full schema for exploratory analyses.

Returns:

Seven-column table with the following fields, ordered as listed—

  • old_stable_id - obsolete identifier (empty string for “birth” events).

  • old_version - version number paired with old_stable_id.

  • new_stable_id - successor identifier (empty string for “retirement” events).

  • new_version - version paired with new_stable_id.

  • score - homology score reported by Ensembl (NaN if unavailable).

  • old_release - Ensembl release where the old identifier last appeared.

  • new_release - release where the new identifier first appeared.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

ValueError – If the identifier delimiter idtrack.DB.id_ver_delimiter is found inside any *_stable_id field, indicating malformed input.

create_ids(form)[source]

Retrieve and normalise raw Ensembl identifier records for the requested molecular form.

This method pulls the appropriate MySQL table(s) for form, copes with schema differences across Ensembl releases (e.g. the historical *_stable_id split tables), coerces data types, and standardises column names so that downstream graph-building steps all consume the same shape. Every id must carry a version (DatabaseManager._require_versions()): a release whose ids have none, or only some, is refused here, so no derived table exists for it.

Parameters:

form (str) – Target molecular form - "gene", "transcript", or "translation". Anything else triggers a ValueError.

Returns:

A de-duplicated, index-reset table whose columns depend on form:

  • gene - gene_id, gene_stable_id, gene_version

  • transcript - transcript_id, gene_id, transcript_stable_id, transcript_version

  • translation - translation_id, transcript_id, translation_stable_id, translation_version

All ID columns are int64 except the *_stable_id strings; version columns are int64.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

ValueError – If ids of the release carry no version (organisms without versioned ids are not supported).

create_relation_current()[source]

Build a current-release gene-transcript-translation mapping table.

The routine fetches the raw stable-ID/​version tables for genes, transcripts and translations via DatabaseManager.get_db(), merges them into a single wide frame, and then delegates to DatabaseManager._create_relation_helper() to harmonise version columns and compress the information into three canonical node labels ("<stable_id>.<version>"). The resulting mapping is the authoritative per-release link between molecular forms and is consumed by downstream graph-building utilities such as idtrack.GraphMaker.construct_graph().

Returns:

Three columns—gene, transcript, and translation—with one row per transcript. The translation column may contain empty strings where non-coding transcripts have no peptide. All data are UTF-8 strings; duplicates are removed and the index is reset.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

create_release_id()[source]

Return deduplicated stable-identifier/version pairs for the current form and release.

Raw identifiers are fetched via DatabaseManager.get_db(), trimmed to the canonical columns, and sanity-checked. Two integrity rules are enforced: (1) the delimiter idtrack.DB.id_ver_delimiter must not appear inside any stable identifier, and (2) every stable identifier must be unique after deduplication. Violations raise ValueError.

Returns:

Two-column dataframe [{form}_stable_id, {form}_version] with duplicates removed.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

ValueError – If the delimiter is present inside any stable identifier or if identifiers are not unique after deduplication.

download_table(table_key, usecols=None)[source]

Download a raw Ensembl MySQL table and return it as a DataFrame.

When the release is on the live Ensembl MySQL service and its port is usable (see idtrack._ensembl_access: the port answered its probe and the access mode is not "https"), the table is selected from the core schema with a server-side cursor (rows are streamed, not held twice); otherwise it is read from Ensembl’s HTTPS dumps (_download_table_from_ftp()). Both routes give the same rows with the same column types: columns of text types (character, enumeration, date and time) are text, the others numbers. Only a failure to reach the MySQL server makes the HTTPS route take over (with a warning that names the cause); a query or data error is raised. Public code is expected to call DatabaseManager.get_table(), which wraps this helper with caching.

Parameters:

  • table_key (str) – Name of the raw table as it appears in the remote Ensembl database (e.g. 'gene', 'mapping_session', 'xref'). Must exist in the schema returned by DatabaseManager.mysql_database().

  • usecols (Optional[list[str]]) – Sequence of column names to project; None retrieves the entire table. Column order is preserved. An empty list is treated the same as None.

Returns:

A frame containing the requested columns in the exact order supplied via

usecols (or all columns if usecols is None). Index is monotonic and zero-based.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

  • EnsemblSchemaError – If the release has no table table_key, or the table lacks an element of usecols (idtrack._db.EnsemblSchemaError).

  • ValueError – If the query returns text that cannot be decoded.

Notes

If the HTTPS dumps cannot be read, idtrack.EnsemblDownloadError propagates.

property external_inst: ExternalDatabases

Instantiate and cache an ExternalDatabases helper for this manager.

The instance mirrors the configuration of the surrounding DatabaseManager—organism, Ensembl release, identifier form, local repository path, and genome assembly—so that all interactions with external data sources remain consistent throughout the session. Because the property is backed by functools.cached_property, the helper is created exactly once and reused on subsequent accesses, eliminating redundant network or file-system look-ups.

Returns:

A lazily created, configuration-matched helper object.

Return type:

ExternalDatabases

get_db(df_indicator, create_even_if_exist=False, save_after_calculation=True)[source]

Return a derived table, from the repository or computed.

Every stored table is kept in a file of its own whose name carries everything the table depends on, so a table computed for one window or externals selection is never served for another:

  • external (all cross references of the form), external_database (row counts per database): keyed by release and form.

  • external_relevant: the rows of the databases the externals YAML enables for this form, assembly and release; keyed by release, form and the sorted list of those databases (its digest in the file name, the list itself in the file, checked on read). external_relevant-database counts its rows (not stored).

  • idhistory and idhistory_narrow: Ensembl’s id history of the release, stored for every mapping session the release records (keyed by release and form) and restricted on reading to the sessions whose old_release lies in the manager’s window.

  • relationcurrent: gene, transcript and translation node names per transcript; keyed by release.

  • Not stored, because they are cheap functions of stored tables: idsraw_<form> (raw ids of form, create_ids()), ids (ids and versions of the manager’s form, create_release_id()), generegion (which genes of the release lie outside the reference sequence, create_gene_region()), externalcontent (create_database_content()) and availabledatabases (create_available_databases()).

Parameters:

  • df_indicator (str) – One of the indicators above.

  • create_even_if_exist (bool) – Compute a stored table again and replace the stored copy.

  • save_after_calculation (bool) – Store a computed table (ignored for the tables that are not stored).

Returns:

The requested table.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

ValueError – If df_indicator is not one of the indicators above.

get_table(table_key, usecols=None, create_even_if_exist=False, save_after_calculation=True)[source]

Return a raw Ensembl table of the manager’s release, from the repository or downloaded.

The table is read from its file in tables_directory if one exists (one file per table, release and column set); otherwise it is downloaded (download_table()) and, if save_after_calculation, stored. A raw table depends only on the release’s core database, so it is shared by every manager of the assembly whatever its form or window.

Parameters:

  • table_key (str) – Name of the MySQL table (e.g. "gene", "xref", "mapping_session").

  • usecols (list[str] | None) – Column subset to retrieve. None (default) selects all columns.

  • create_even_if_exist (bool) – Download the table even if it is stored, and replace the stored copy.

  • save_after_calculation (bool) – Store a downloaded table.

Returns:

The requested raw table, its columns in the order of usecols when given, otherwise in

the schema’s order.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

ValueError – If usecols is an empty list or not a list.

id_ver_from_df(dbm_the_ids)[source]

Assemble fully qualified node names from a stable-ID / version DataFrame.

This convenience routine converts a two-column frame—usually produced by DatabaseManager.get_db() with the ids form—into the canonical node labels used throughout ID-track graphs (e.g. ENSG00000000001.1). It first validates that the input columns match self._identifiers (typically ["gene_stable_id", "gene_version"] or analogous for the current form), then delegates per-row processing to DatabaseManager.node_dict_maker() and DatabaseManager.node_name_maker(). The resulting list may be fed directly into downstream graph builders or written to disk for later reuse.

Parameters:

dbm_the_ids (pandas.DataFrame) – Two-column frame containing the stable identifiers and their Ensembl version numbers. The column order and names must exactly match self._identifiers; otherwise an exception is raised.

Returns:

Ordered list where each element is "<ID>.<version>"; for a row

without version (the empty id of a transcript that has no translation) the id itself.

Return type:

list[str]

Raises:

ValueError – If dbm_the_ids does not contain the expected column names stored in self._identifiers.

property mysql_database: str

Return the canonical Ensembl Core schema name for the current organism, release, and assembly.

The schema naming convention is deterministic:

{organism}_core_{ensembl_release}_{DbSuffix}[<patch>]

where DbSuffix is the assembly’s core-database code (idtrack.DB.db_suffix(), usually the assembly key itself).

For multi-port assemblies (e.g. sus_scrofa assembly 102), the port is selected in __init__() using _get_core_db_index(). Once the release is validated to exist on that chosen port, the schema name itself does not require another server-side discovery query.

Returns:

Schema name like "homo_sapiens_core_111_38".

Return type:

str

Raises:

ValueError – If the current release is not available for this (organism, assembly) pair.

static node_dict_maker(id_entry, version_entry)[source]

Return a normalized ID/Version dictionary from raw column values.

This helper creates the canonical structure consumed by DatabaseManager.node_name_maker() and higher-level graph utilities, ensuring that version numbers are strictly integers whenever possible. It also recognises special placeholders defined in idtrack.DB.alternative_versions (e.g. "Retired" or "Void") and passes them through unchanged so that downstream code can handle deprecated or missing entries appropriately.

Parameters:

  • id_entry (str) – Stable identifier portion preceding the delimiter (e.g. "ENSG00000000001").

  • version_entry (Any) – Raw version value following the delimiter (e.g. 1 in "ENSG00000000001.1"). May be float, int, str, None, NaN, or an alternative placeholder such as "Retired".

Returns:

{"ID": id_entry, "Version": version_entry} with Version coerced to int when it represents a whole number.

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

Raises:

ValueError – If version_entry is numeric but contains a fractional component (e.g. 1.2), indicating a malformed identifier that cannot be represented as an integer version.

static node_name_maker(node_dict)[source]

Concatenate ID and Version into a single node label.

Given the miniature dictionary returned by DatabaseManager.node_dict_maker(), this helper builds the string representation that uniquely identifies a biological entity within the graph layer. It appends the version (a number, or one of the markers of idtrack.DB.alternative_versions) to the stable ID using idtrack.DB.id_ver_delimiter ("." by default). An entry without version is an absent identifier (the empty id of a transcript that has no translation) and is returned as it is.

Parameters:

node_dict (dict[str, Any]) – Mapping with exactly two keys, "ID" and "Version", as produced by DatabaseManager.node_dict_maker().

Returns:

"<ID>.<version>", or "<ID>" for an entry without version.

Return type:

str

The digests identify the tables’ content (idtrack._utils_hdf5.read_table_digest()), so that a graph can record what it was built from.

class ExternalDatabases(organism, ensembl_release, form, local_repository, genome_assembly)[source]

Bases: object

Manage third-party metadata for Ensembl entities through YAML side-car files.

This helper encapsulates everything related to the external (i.e. non-Ensembl) databases that can be linked to a given organism, genome assembly, release, and biological form (gene / transcript / translation). Examples of such resources include ArrayExpress, RefSeq, Uniprot, HGNC, and dozens of smaller annotation providers. Rather than hard-coding those relationships, the wider ID-Track toolkit stores them in a human-readable YAML file that lives next to the local data cache managed by _database_manager.DatabaseManager.

The YAML workflow is:

  1. create_template_yaml() enumerates every known combination and writes a template where each entry is marked Include: false.

  2. A user (or an automated post-processing step) reviews the template, toggling Include to true for the resources they need.

  3. The modified YAML is saved under local_repository; subsequent calls to load_modified_yaml() return it as a plain dict for downstream logic.

  4. Every file is checked when it is read (validate_externals_yaml(): boolean Include, assembly keys and releases that the organism table allows), and validate_yaml_file_up_to_date() raises ExternalsReleaseNotCoveredError if the manager’s release is not listed at all (extend_modified_yaml() adds new releases).

  5. Utility helpers such as give_list_for_case() expose convenient filtered views—e.g. all databases that should be downloaded for the current form, or all releases supported by assembly 38.

In short, ExternalDatabases provides a single, version-controlled “contract” describing which third-party tables belong in an ID-track run, while granting users explicit opt-in control over optional resources.

Instantiate a YAML controller tied to a specific organism, release, and assembly.

The constructor mirrors the core configuration of _database_manager.DatabaseManager so that both objects operate on the exact same coordinate system. No I/O is performed at construction time; paths are merely recorded, and loggers are configured. Heavy-weight actions—such as scanning the cache for existing YAMLs or writing new ones—happen lazily when the corresponding methods are called.

Parameters:

  • organism (str) – Canonical Ensembl species identifier in snake_case (e.g. "homo_sapiens"), exactly as in idtrack.DB.supported_organisms.

  • ensembl_release (int) – Target Ensembl release number (e.g. 110). Must correspond to a release that actually exists for organism and genome_assembly.

  • form (str) – Entity level—"gene", "transcript", or "translation". Any other value raises ValueError in higher-level validation.

  • local_repository (str) – Writable directory where YAML files and downloads are cached. The directory need not pre-exist; if missing, most public methods will attempt to create it.

  • genome_assembly (int) – Assembly key of idtrack.DB.assembly_mysqlport_priority (e.g. 38 = human GRCh38, 37 = human GRCh37, 39 = mouse GRCm39, 111 = pig Sscrofa11.1, 10 = rhesus Mmul_10). The YAML’s assembly keys are these keys. Used to disambiguate multiple assemblies available for the same organism/release pair.

create_template_yaml(df)[source]

Generate a template YAML enumerating external-database options.

This helper scans df—typically the dataframe returned by idtrack.DatabaseManager.create_database_content()—and writes a scaffold configuration file to file_name_template_yaml(). The file lists every organism → form → database combination observed in df, grouped by genome assembly and Ensembl release. For each entry the template records whether the database should be included when building an ID-history graph, its integer Database Index, and an empty Potential Synonymous placeholder that future versions may use to flag overlapping resources.

Users are expected to edit the generated file—changing Include from false to true where appropriate—and rename it by appending _modified to the filename before the package will load it. A warning to that effect is emitted via logging.Logger.warning().

The resulting YAML resembles the structure below (truncated for brevity):

homo_sapiens:
    gene:
        ArrayExpress:
            Assembly:
                "37":
                    Ensembl release: 79,80,81,82,83,84,85,86,87,88,89
                    Include: false
                "38":
                    Ensembl release: 79,80,81,82,83,84,85,86,87,88,89
                    Include: false
            Database Index: 0
            Potential Synonymous: ""
        Clone-based (Ensembl):
            Assembly:
                "37":
                    Ensembl release: 79,80,81,82,83,84,85
                    Include: false
                "38":
                    Ensembl release: 79,80,81,82,83,84,85
                    Include: false
            Database Index: 5
            Potential Synonymous: ""

Editing guidelines

  • Set Include to true for every assembly of the databases you need.

  • Save the edited file with _modified appended to the base name so that downstream routines load the customised version.

Parameters:

df (pandas.DataFrame) – Dataframe containing at least the columns ["organism", "form", "name_db", "assembly", "release"]. It should be produced by idtrack.DatabaseManager.create_database_content() so that the expected schema is guaranteed.

Notes

The Potential Synonymous is now all empty. In the following versions, it is aimed to integrate a feature that prevent to heve synonymous databases in the list. Likewise, Database Index has now no use case, in the program. It is important to follow the final warning raised by the method. ‘’Please edit the file based on requested external databases and add ‘_modified’ to the file name.’’. The editing should be done by converting Include sections from false to true. It is recommended to make the change for each assembly for a given database.

extend_modified_yaml(content, output_path=None, base_path=None)[source]

Extend the organism’s modified externals YAML to the releases of a database-content table.

This is the way to bring an existing <organism>_externals_modified.yml up to new Ensembl releases without regenerating and re-curating it. content is the output of idtrack.DatabaseManager.create_database_content() for the new releases (build the manager with ignore_before and ignore_after set to them). For every (form, database, assembly) that content holds:

  • an existing entry gets the new releases added to its Ensembl release list, and keeps its Include flag;

  • a database that the file does not have yet is added with Include: false and reported under "new_databases", so that a person can decide whether to enable it;

  • a known database that appears with a new assembly gets an entry for that assembly. Its Include flag is true only if the database is Include: true on every assembly it already has (the database is then enabled as a whole, as in the shipped files); otherwise it is false. All such entries are reported under "new_assembly_entries", and the ones switched on, which no person has reviewed, are listed again under "switched_on" and in a warning.

The base file is base_path if given, else the local repository’s copy if present, else the shipped default. The result is written to output_path (default: <local_repository>/<organism>_externals_modified.yml), in the layout of the shipped files, atomically (comments of the base file are not kept). When the file read is replaced, its previous version is kept as <file>.bak. Passing a template as both base_path and output_path extends the template the same way (all its flags are false).

Parameters:

  • content (DataFrame) – Frame with at least the columns organism, form, name_db, assembly and release; rows of other organisms are ignored.

  • output_path (str | None) – Where to write the extended file.

  • base_path (str | None) – File to extend instead of the modified YAML that load_modified_yaml() would read.

Returns:

Report with keys "path" (file written), "releases" (releases of content), "extended_entries" (number of existing entries that gained releases), "new_databases" (list of (form, database, assembly)), "new_assembly_entries" (list of (form, database, assembly, include)) and "switched_on" (list of (form, database, assembly) of the new assembly entries added with Include: true).

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

Raises:

ValueError – If content lacks a required column or has no row for the organism.

file_name_modified_yaml(mode)[source]

Resolve the path to a modified YAML file customised by the user or shipped with the package.

The method supports two modes that map to different storage locations:

  • "configured" - the user-edited file living in ExternalDatabases.local_repository.

  • "default" - the read-only fallback bundled under <package_root>/default_config for quick starts and unit tests.

By funnelling every lookup through this routine, higher-level helpers such as ExternalDatabases.load_modified_yaml() remain agnostic about the underlying directory structure and can focus on validation and parsing instead.

Parameters:

mode (str) – Either "configured" or "default" selecting the corresponding search location.

Returns:

Absolute path of the requested YAML file.

Return type:

str

Raises:

ValueError – If mode is not one of the recognised values.

file_name_template_yaml()[source]

Return absolute path to the template YAML configuration file.

A helper that deterministically builds the filename used by ExternalDatabases.create_template_yaml() when it first scaffolds the external-database configuration for organism. Centralising the logic here keeps every component of idtrack that may need the path (tests, CLI tools, future maintenance scripts) in perfect sync with a single implementation. The method performs no I/O; it merely concatenates ExternalDatabases.local_repository and the conventional filename pattern "<organism>_externals_template.yml" so callers can decide whether to create, read, or overwrite the file.

Returns:

Absolute path of <organism>_externals_template.yml located inside ExternalDatabases.local_repository.

Return type:

str

give_list_for_case(give_type)[source]

Return database names or assembly codes extracted from the external-DB YAML file.

The helper provides a lightweight way for higher-level components (e.g. DatabaseManager) to discover which external resources—or which genome assemblies—are currently eligible according to the user-editable YAML configuration created by ExternalDatabases.create_template_yaml(). Instead of forcing the caller to parse the YAML structure manually, the method filters the entries for the manager’s organism, form, Ensembl release and genome assembly and returns the requested slice.

Parameters:

give_type (str) –

Kind of list to return. Accepted values are

  • "db" external-database names (str) whose Include flag is true for the current organism, form, assembly and Ensembl release.

  • "assembly" genome-assembly codes (int) for which the YAML enables at least one external database (Include: true) at the current Ensembl release, restricted to the assemblies whose release window (organism table) holds that release.

Returns:

  • When give_type is "db", a list of database names.

  • When give_type is "assembly", a list of assembly codes.

Return type:

list[str] | list[int]

Raises:

ValueError – If give_type is not "db" nor "assembly" or if an unexpected internal inconsistency is encountered while traversing the YAML structure.

load_modified_yaml()[source]

Load the user-edited or default YAML configuration and verify release compatibility.

This convenience wrapper searches for the configured YAML file first; if it does not exist or lacks read permissions a warning is logged and the default YAML file shipped with the package is tried instead. Failure to locate either file aborts with a FileNotFoundError that names the file to create and the documented way to create it. After loading, the method delegates to ExternalDatabases.validate_yaml_file_up_to_date() to ensure that the currently requested Ensembl release is represented in the configuration.

Returns:

Parsed YAML content keyed by {organism → form → database → Assembly → {...}}.

Return type:

dict

read_modified_yaml()[source]

Read the modified YAML (local repository first, then the shipped default) without release checks.

The file is parsed and checked against the organism table once per version of the file (load_externals_yaml()).

class VerifyOrganism(organism_query)[source]

Bases: object

Resolve a tentative organism identifier to the formal Ensembl species name and its latest supported release.

The class shields end-users from the quirks of the Ensembl REST payload by converting any synonym—common name, scientific name, assembly name or accession, or NCBI taxon ID—into the canonical Ensembl species identifier (e.g. homo_sapiens) and the newest Ensembl release that still hosts that species. Matching is case-insensitive on both sides. A query equal to a formal name (also written with spaces, e.g. "Macaca mulatta") or to a taxon ID is never ambiguous: a taxon ID that Ensembl also gives to strains or breeds resolves to the species-level entry (9823 → sus_scrofa). Any other synonym that several species share raises an error that lists the candidates, unless idtrack declares it as the alias of one organism (idtrack.DB.organism_aliases: "pig", "human", "mouse", "rhesus", "cynomolgus"; Ensembl lists "pig" as the common name of every pig breed).

The species list comes from one call to the Ensembl REST API per process and day (/info/species, see idtrack._ensembl_access.rest_get_json() and idtrack.DB.rest_species_cache_seconds), made only when it is needed: the formal name of an organism configured in idtrack (idtrack.DB.supported_organisms, also written with spaces) and its declared aliases resolve without the network; other synonyms, taxon IDs and the latest release need it.

After construction the instance offers two high-level helpers:

>>> resolver = VerifyOrganism("human")
>>> resolver.get_formal_name()      # 'homo_sapiens'
>>> resolver.get_latest_release()   # 117  (example)

Both helpers are backed by two public dataframes, loaded on first use:

  • name_synonyms_dataframe — maps every synonym returned by the REST service to the chosen formal name and flags synonyms that are ambiguous across species.

  • ensembl_release_dataframe — one row per Ensembl species (indexed by formal_name) holding its latest Ensembl release number.

The names of the assemblies of the organism table (also of earlier assemblies, e.g. "GRCh37") resolve to their organism without the network; they name the organism, not the assembly. A malformed species entry of Ensembl is left out with a warning, unless it is one of idtrack’s organisms (then it is an error).

Initialise the resolver; nothing is fetched until a look-up needs the Ensembl species list.

Parameters:

organism_query (str | int) – Organism identifier supplied by the user—common name ("human"), shorthand ("hsapiens"), taxon ID (9606 or "9606"), assembly name ("Mmul_10"), or Ensembl species name ("homo_sapiens", "Macaca mulatta"). The value is converted to a stripped, lower-case string before processing.

_configured_formal_name()[source]

Return the configured organism the query names without the network, else None.

The query names a configured organism when it is its formal name (also with spaces or hyphens), one of its declared aliases (idtrack.DB.organism_aliases: "pig", "human"; a declared alias wins over whatever Ensembl lists under the same word) or the name of one of its assemblies in the organism table ("GRCh37", "Sscrofa10.2", "Mmul_8.0.1"; matched case-insensitively). An assembly name resolves the organism only; it does not select that assembly.

Returns:

The organism’s formal name, or None.

Return type:

Optional[str]

Return the species tables of this process.

They are fetched at the first need and again once they are older than idtrack.DB.rest_species_cache_seconds, so that a long-running process learns of a new release.

See fetch_organism_and_latest_release().

Return type:

Query the Ensembl REST API once and build lookup tables for species synonyms and latest releases.

This internal utility performs a single call to /info/species on the Ensembl REST server, parses the returned JSON, and constructs two pandas dataframes:

  • name_synonyms_df - one row per (normalised synonym, species), with columns synonym,

    formal_name, kind ("formal_name", "taxon_id" or "other") and ambiguous (True if the synonym belongs to more than one species).

  • latest_ensembl_releases_df - indexed by formal_name and holding a single ensembl_release

    integer column.

The request uses the timeouts and retries of idtrack._ensembl_access.rest_get_json(), whose idtrack.EnsemblRestError propagates when Ensembl does not answer (idtrack.DB.connection_timeout, idtrack.DB.reading_timeout, idtrack.DB.rest_attempts). _species_tables() keeps the result for the process.

get_formal_name()[source]

Resolve the user’s organism query to the canonical Ensembl species name.

Resolution, in this order (all comparisons on normalised, lower-case strings):

  1. the query is a formal name ("homo_sapiens"), also with spaces or hyphens for underscores ("Macaca mulatta"), or an alias that idtrack declares for an organism ("pig"); for an organism configured in idtrack this needs no network;

  2. the query is a taxon ID: the organism with that ID, or—when Ensembl gives the ID to several strains or breeds—the species-level entry (the formal name of two words, sus_scrofa for 9823);

  3. any other synonym of name_synonyms_dataframe (common names, display names, assembly names and accessions, aliases), which must belong to exactly one organism.

Returns:

The canonical Ensembl species identifier (always lower-case, e.g. "homo_sapiens").

Return type:

str

Raises:

  • ValueError – If the query matches more than one organism (an ambiguous synonym); the message lists the candidates.

Down-stream routines (e.g. database connectors, file download helpers) rely on this value to decide which Ensembl release to fetch, ensuring the entire pipeline stays on a single, internally consistent genome build.

class ConnectionBridge(proxy_host='127.0.0.1', proxy_port=1080, *, set_env_proxy=True)[source]

Bases: object

Route this Python process’ outgoing TCP connections through an SSH-provided SOCKS proxy.

Many restricted environments block outbound internet access from compute nodes. IDTrack needs outbound access to Ensembl services (REST/HTTPS, FTP over HTTPS, and sometimes public MySQL). If you can SSH into the server from a machine with internet access, you can expose a SOCKS5 proxy on the server via OpenSSH remote dynamic forwarding:

ssh -R 1080 user@server

Then, inside Python on the server (or inside a Jupyter notebook kernel running on the server), enable the bridge:

import idtrack

b = idtrack.ConnectionBridge(proxy_port=1080)
b.start()  # applies process-scoped networking changes

# ... run IDTrack ...

b.stop()   # restores the previous networking configuration

Internals (for maintainers / power users)

start() monkeypatches socket.socket to socks.socksocket (PySocks) and optionally sets the environment variables ALL_PROXY and all_proxy so subprocesses spawned from this process inherit the proxy.

A private, process-wide _BridgeState singleton stores the original socket class, environment variables, and PySocks default proxy to ensure stop() can restore the prior state precisely. The singleton also implements a simple reference counter so multiple ConnectionBridge instances can share the same active bridge.

Notes

  • The bridge affects only the current Python process (one Jupyter kernel). Closing the Python process/kernel automatically removes the monkeypatch. It is not undone when the instance is garbage-collected: stop() of the instance (or the end of its with block), stop_all() or the end of the process undo it.

  • The with ConnectionBridge(...): form raises ConnectionError when the connectivity check fails, so the block never runs unbridged.

  • To avoid surprises, call start() before the first network access in your program.

  • Status messages are emitted via the logger named "connection_bridge" and, when verbose=True, printed to stdout for immediate visibility in notebooks.

param proxy_host:

SOCKS proxy host on the server. With ssh -R 1080 ... this is typically "127.0.0.1".

param proxy_port:

SOCKS proxy port on the server. Must match the port used in the SSH command.

param set_env_proxy:

If True (default), set ALL_PROXY/all_proxy while active so subprocesses inherit the proxy configuration.

Create a new bridge controller without applying any network changes.

How idtrack reaches Ensembl: the access mode and the per-process reachability of TCP ports.

Ensembl serves the same core databases two ways: the public MySQL service (ensembldb.ensembl.org, ports 3306, 5306 and 3337) and the MySQL dumps on https://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/. Many networks block the MySQL ports, and a blocked port costs a full connect timeout every time it is tried. This module makes that cost a one-off:

  • ensembl_access_mode() returns the access mode, "auto" (MySQL where its port answers, the HTTPS dumps otherwise) or "https" (MySQL is never touched), from idtrack.DB.ensembl_access or the IDTRACK_ENSEMBL_ACCESS environment variable.

  • reachability (a PortReachability) probes a (host, port) once per process with a short timeout and remembers the answer. Every code path that would open a MySQL connection asks it first, and a connection that fails after a successful probe marks the port unreachable for the rest of the process.

  • rest_get_json() is the one way idtrack asks Ensembl REST, and https_get() the one way it reads the HTTPS dumps: both with the timeouts of idtrack.DB.connection_timeout and idtrack.DB.reading_timeout, the same retries, and an error that says what failed and what to change (idtrack.EnsemblRestError, EnsemblDownloadError). https_get() tells “absent” (HTTP 404 or 410 from a server that answered) apart from “unknown” (time-out, connection error, 429, 5xx), which is retried and, if it stays unknown, raised: a failed request is never read as “does not exist”.

The results do not depend on the mode: both paths read the same Ensembl tables, with the same column types.

class PortReachability[source]

Remember, per process, whether a TCP (host, port) accepts connections.

The first question about a (host, port) opens one TCP connection with a short timeout (idtrack.DB.mysql_probe_timeout unless given); later questions are answered from memory. mark_unreachable() records a failure observed elsewhere: a MySQL connection that fails after a successful probe (refused, dropped or lost during a query) marks the port unreachable. A “reachable” answer is kept for the life of the process; an “unreachable” one expires, so that a long-running process does not stay on the slower HTTPS dumps for days after one network blip: after retry_after_seconds (10 minutes) the port is probed again, and every further failure doubles the wait, up to max_retry_after_seconds (one day). The memory is process-wide, so parallel requests do not each wait for a probe. Unreachable ports only cost speed: the tables are then read from the HTTPS dumps, which hold the same rows. reset() forgets everything, which is needed when the network route changes inside a process (as idtrack.ConnectionBridge does when it starts or stops).

Create an empty reachability memory.

Read Ensembl’s MySQL table dumps (<table>.txt.gz) exactly as MySQL would load them.

The dumps are written by SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE with the default FIELDS TERMINATED BY '\t' ESCAPED BY '\\' LINES TERMINATED BY '\n'. In that format a backslash escapes the next character: a field that holds a tab or a newline is written as a backslash followed by the raw tab or newline, a backslash as \\, NUL as \0, and SQL NULL as a field consisting of \N. LOAD DATA also reads \b, \n, \r, \t and \Z as backspace, newline, carriage return, tab and Ctrl-Z. Any other escaped character stands for itself. Raw carriage returns are ordinary data (only \n ends a record).

Reading such a file with a plain tab-separated parser splits a record at every escaped newline, keeps the escaping backslashes and treats a leading double quote as CSV quoting. read_mysql_dump() instead decodes each record the way LOAD DATA does and hands pandas an unambiguous CSV stream, so the frame matches what the MySQL server returns for the same table (NULL becomes NaN; pandas infers the column dtypes as it does for any text input). Records without escapes or quotes, the vast majority, pass through untouched.

class MySQLDumpCSVStream(source, chunk_size=1048576)[source]

Text stream that turns a MySQL dump into CSV that pandas parses unambiguously.

Records are read from source (a text stream of the dump) and written out as tab-separated CSV records: records without backslash escapes or double quotes are passed through; the others are decoded field by field, and fields containing a tab, newline or double quote are quoted. SQL NULL stays \N (read by pandas as NaN through na_values). Values that pandas cannot reproduce verbatim are emitted as empty fields and recorded in restore as (record index, field index, value) for read_mysql_dump() to put back.

Parameters:

  • source (Any) – Readable text stream of the dump (already decompressed).

  • chunk_size (int) – Number of characters read from source at a time.

Wrap source; nothing is read until read() is called.

Allowlists of the externals YAML files shipped in idtrack/default_config.

A shipped <organism>_externals_modified.yml is the organism’s template (made by idtrack.DatabaseManager.create_database_content() and idtrack.ExternalDatabases.create_template_yaml() over every release and form) with Include: true set for the (form, database, assembly) entries of the organism’s allowlist below, by apply_allowlist(). Nothing else differs between template and modified file. The lists follow one conceptual set for every organism, with the species’ own symbol databases:

  • gene: clone-based, Havana and Vega names, EntrezGene / NCBI gene, RFAM, UniProtKB gene names, the species’ symbol source(s), and the synonym_id:: forms of the identifier and symbol databases;

  • transcript: CCDS, Havana transcripts and RefSeq mRNA / ncRNA (curated and predicted);

  • translation: Havana translations, RefSeq peptides (curated and predicted) and UniProt (Swiss-Prot, TrEMBL).

Names that an organism’s template does not contain are skipped. Tutorial 02 (docs/_notebooks/02_prepare_new_external_yaml.ipynb) shows the same lists as editable dictionaries.

Storage of idtrack’s cached tables: one immutable HDF5 file per table, written atomically.

Every table that idtrack.DatabaseManager downloads or computes is kept in a file of its own (<directory>/<table key>.h5). A table is written completely to a private temporary file in the same directory, flushed to disk and only then renamed to its final name (os.replace(), atomic on POSIX file systems), so:

  • a table that is visible is complete: a process killed in the middle of a write (time limit, out of memory, closed kernel) leaves the repository as it was, apart from an orphaned temporary file that no reader ever opens;

  • finished files are never opened for writing again, so readers need no lock and are never blocked by writers, and two processes that compute the same table at the same time both succeed (the last rename wins, with a complete table);

  • replacing a table frees the space of the old one (there is no in-file deletion that HDF5 cannot reclaim).

Each file records the storage format version and the parameters the table was computed with (write_table()); load_table() returns a table only if both match what the caller asks for, so a table made under other parameters is never served.

The format stores every column by position (labels and dtypes are metadata), text as dictionary codes plus the distinct values as one compressed UTF-8 byte buffer with offsets (missing values are code -1, never a sentinel string), categoricals as codes plus categories, datetimes and timedeltas as int64 with their exact unit, and numbers and booleans as they are, all chunked with the shuffle filter and gzip level 4. A table read back equals the table written (DataFrame.equals and identical dtypes; text comes back in the default text dtype of the running pandas, object under pandas 2 and str under pandas 3, with NaN for missing values, which is what pandas produces for freshly computed text). Files are written with the HDF5 format bounds ("earliest", "v110"), so a file written with any HDF5 library from 1.10 on is readable by every other.

TABLE_FORMAT_VERSION = 2

Version of the on-disk table format; a file of another version is not read (the table is recomputed).

exception TableFormatError[source]

A table cannot be stored in, or read from, idtrack’s table format.

Self-tests

class TrackTests(*args, **kwargs)[source]

Bases: Track, ABC

The self-tests of a graph: checks that compare a built graph with Ensembl’s tables and with itself.

A TrackTests is a Track with a database manager (it reads the tables the graph was built from) and two groups of methods, for developers and for the end of a graph build. Nothing here changes the graph.

Checks (is_...). Each states one invariant of a built graph and returns a idtrack._track_tests.CheckResult: whether the invariant holds, and what was compared and found. A check does not raise for what it finds: a violation is a result that does not hold, and so is anything that keeps the check from being completed (a table that cannot be read, a release without identifiers), with the error in the result’s details. So the checks can be run one after the other, and a result is never mistaken for success: its truth value is the verdict.

Conversion runs (history_...). They convert the identifiers of a database at a release and count what happened to them; they return the counts and raise ValueError for arguments that cannot be used.

A database that the graph does not hold is refused before anything is searched, by the checks and the conversion runs alike and as idtrack.API refuses a wrong argument: a ValueError that names the argument and lists what is valid (a TypeError for a value that is not a string).

Ensembl keeps one genome assembly per release as the primary one, and an earlier assembly can stay listed beside it (human GRCh37). A release therefore exists per assembly: the checks ask the manager for an assembly first and for the release second, and compare assembly by assembly.

Typical use:

api.build_graph("homo_sapiens", 115, return_test=True)
result = api.track.is_id_functions_consistent_ensembl()
if not result:
    print(result.details)
details_limit

How many examples of each kind of violation a result keeps (the number found is always reported).

Type:

int

random_draw_attempts

How often the random arguments of a conversion run are drawn before history_travel_testing_random_arguments_generator() gives up.

Type:

int

history_travel_testing(from_release, from_assembly, from_database, to_release, to_database, go_external, prioritize_to_one_filter, convert_using_release, from_fraction=1.0, verbose=True, verbose_detailed=False, return_ensembl_alternative=False)[source]

Run an end-to-end Ensembl-history conversion and collect granular QA metrics.

The routine samples identifiers from from_database/from_release (optionally down-sampling via from_fraction) and converts each one to to_database/to_release using idtrack.Track.convert(). It is intentionally non-fatal: every failure mode is caught, logged and tallied so that large regression suites can run unattended. All results are returned in a single nested metrics dictionary whose structure mirrors the printable report produced by format_history_travel_testing_report().

The statistics fall into four conceptual groups; each counter not only records an absolute event count but also serves as a red-flag indicator for specific classes of mapping pathology. Use the guidelines below to interpret the numbers and decide whether a run is healthy, questionable, or action-required.

  • Failure / anomaly counters

    • history_voyage_failed_gracefully - the converter declined with one of its two named errors: idtrack.InactiveAtReleaseError (the id is not active in the graph at the release it was taken from) or idtrack.SearchBudgetExceededError.

    • history_voyage_failed_unknown - any other unexpected exception.

    • query_not_in_the_graph - source ID absent from the graph.

    • lost_item - traversal finished but produced no final IDs.

    • lost_item_but_the_same_id_exists - special case of lost_item when the target and source DB are both Ensembl-gene and the target ID still exists in the graph.

    • found_ids_not_accurate - at least one returned target ID is not part of the authoritative ids_to reference set.

  • Mapping quality

    • one_to_one_ids - queries that resolved to exactly one target ID.

    • one_to_multiple_ids - queries with > 1 admissible targets.

    • one_to_multiple_final_conversion - subset of the above where exactly one traversal path was found (heuristics eliminated alternatives).

  • Collision analysis

    The list clashing_id_type == [clash_one_one, clash_multi_multi, clash_multi_one] classifies target IDs that were reached by more than one query:

    • clash_one_one - every colliding query was 1→1.

    • clash_multi_multi - every colliding query was 1→many.

    • clash_multi_one - mixture of 1→1 and 1→many queries (most alarming category).

  • Timings & book-keeping

    • time - wall-clock runtime in seconds.

    • conversion - per-query mapping result for all successful traversals.

    • converted_item_dict / converted_item_dict_reversed - raw per-ID caches used to derive the higher-level counters above.

    • parameters - echo of the function arguments.

    • ids - the sampled from and reference to ID sets.

Parameters:

  • from_release (int) – Ensembl release number of the source IDs.

  • from_assembly (int) – Genome assembly code of the source IDs.

  • from_database (str) – Node-type / database of the source IDs.

  • to_release (int) – Ensembl release number of the target IDs.

  • to_database (str) – Node-type / database to convert into.

  • go_external (bool) – Permit temporary detours through external IDs when native Ensembl history edges break.

  • prioritize_to_one_filter (bool) – Prefer 1→1 mappings over 1→many when multiple paths exist.

  • convert_using_release (bool) – Pass from_release straight into idtrack.Track.convert() instead of letting it infer the starting point.

  • from_fraction (float) – Fraction (0 < x ≤ 1) of the ids_from population to sample; speeds up smoke tests.

  • verbose (bool) – Show tqdm progress bar (coarse).

  • verbose_detailed (bool) – Embed live metric counters in the tqdm postfix.

  • return_ensembl_alternative (bool) – Forwarded to idtrack.Track.convert().

Raises:

  • ValueError – If a database is not one that the graph holds; nothing is converted then, and the message lists what is valid. A source is an external database of from_assembly or the Ensembl ids of a form of the graph, named by their node type (ensembl_gene, base_ensembl_gene, or assembly_<key>_ensembl_<form> for the ids of that assembly; the name of a form, gene, is not a database). A target is a database that idtrack.Track.convert() takes as final_database at to_release (idtrack.Track.final_databases()). Also if to_release is not a release of the graph, or from_fraction is outside the interval (0, 1].

  • TypeError – If a database is not a string.

Returns:

Nested metrics dictionary with the layout described above.

Use format_history_travel_testing_report() for a human-readable summary.

Return type:

dict

Notes

  • All counters are absolute counts - divide by len(metrics['ids']['from']) to obtain rates.

  • The collision analysis is inspired by the clash statistics logic implemented at the end of the function and helps spot discrepant “unique” IDs that suddenly become ambiguous. Keeping all three clash counters at zero is the gold standard for a healthy build.

how_many_corresponding_path_ensembl(from_release, from_assembly, to_release, go_external, verbose=True)[source]

Count history paths between two Ensembl releases.

The method iterates over all Ensembl-gene stable IDs that exist in from_release/from_assembly. For every ID that is present in the graph it calls idtrack.Track.get_possible_paths() and records how many distinct paths the searcher finds to to_release.

The routine is non-destructive; it merely provides a quick way to gauge the density of the history graph or to spot releases where path-finding was unexpectedly difficult.

Parameters:

  • from_release (int) – Source Ensembl release number.

  • from_assembly (int) – Source genome assembly code.

  • to_release (int) – Target Ensembl release number.

  • go_external (bool) – If True history paths are allowed to temporarily leave the Ensembl lineage via external databases.

  • verbose (bool) – Show a tqdm progress bar (default True).

Returns:

A list of two-element sub-lists [stable_id, n_paths] where n_paths is

  • an int ≥ 0 when the ID was in the graph, or

  • None when the source ID was absent.

Return type:

list[list[Union[str, int, None]]]

is_base_is_range_correct(verbose=True)[source]

Check that a gene id without version exists exactly where one of its versions does.

For every gene id without version two ways of saying where it exists must agree:

  1. the releases of the edges from the id to its versions, on any assembly (idtrack.TheGraph.combined());

  2. the union of the releases of its versions on any assembly (idtrack.TheGraph.get_active_ranges_of_base_id_alternative(), which also refuses a version whose edges contradict its history; that is reported as a difference too).

Parameters:

verbose (bool) – Show a progress bar.

Returns:

details: compared (the number of gene ids), n_differing and differing (per gene id its id, the ranges of its edges and of its versions, or the contradiction of a version).

Return type:

CheckResult

is_combined_summary_complete()[source]

Check that every node has a summary of its cross-reference edges, except the two placeholders of an id.

idtrack.TheGraph.combined() sums what the cross-reference edges of a node say, by the kind of the node (the edges that enter a gene, the edges that leave any other node). Every node of a built graph has such edges, with two exceptions by construction: <id>.Void and <id>.Retired, the nodes that stand for “before the id existed” and “after it was retired”, which only the history touches.

Returns:

details: compared (the number of nodes), n_without_summary and without_summary (nodes that no cross-reference edge touches, or whose summary is empty), n_placeholders_with_summary and placeholders_with_summary.

Return type:

CheckResult

is_edge_with_same_nts_only_at_backbone_nodes()[source]

Check that only genes of the backbone are linked to nodes of their own type.

The graph has layers: the history links gene versions of the backbone with each other; every other edge links nodes of two different types (an external identifier and a gene, a transcript and its gene, a gene id without version and its versions). An edge between two nodes of one type that is not the backbone’s is a violation.

Returns:

details: compared (the number of nodes), n_same_type and same_type (pairs of linked nodes of one type that is not the backbone’s, with the type).

Return type:

CheckResult

is_final_external_conversion_robust(convert_using_release=False, database=None, ens_rel=None, verbose=True, from_fraction=1.0, prioritize_to_one_filter=False)[source]

Check that every gene of a release converts to the ids that an external database gives it there.

The genes of a release are converted, at that release, into an external database that attaches its ids to genes, and each conversion is compared with the manager’s table of external identifiers of the assembly that serves the release. The invariant holds when every gene that the table gives an id converts to exactly those ids (letter case ignored), and no gene converts to an id that the table does not give it. A gene without an id in the database converts to nothing; that is the only loss that is not a violation.

Parameters:

  • convert_using_release (bool) – Give the release to the conversion as from_release (otherwise the engine chooses where the gene id is read).

  • database (str | None) – The external database. None: drawn at random among the external databases that attach ids to genes (at ens_rel, when that is given).

  • ens_rel (int | None) – The Ensembl release. None: drawn at random among the releases at which the database has ids (of any such database, when database is None too).

  • verbose (bool) – Show a progress bar and log what is tested.

  • from_fraction (float) – The fraction of the genes that is converted (0 < x <= 1).

  • prioritize_to_one_filter (bool) – Convert with the engine’s best answer only.

Returns:

details: database, assembly, release, compared (the number of genes converted), and four kinds of violation, each with its number (n_...) and first examples: different (converted to other ids than the table’s: id, converted, expected), unexpected (converted although the table gives the gene no id), lost_with_id (not converted although the table gives the gene an id) and failed (the conversion raised). Also lost (every gene that was not converted, with or without an id in the table) and run (the counts of history_travel_testing()). A check that could not be made (no database and release to draw, a release at which the database has no ids, a release the graph does not have) does not hold and says why in error.

Return type:

CheckResult

Raises:

  • ValueError – If database is not an external database of the graph that attaches its ids to genes; nothing is converted then, and the message lists what is valid.

  • TypeError – If database is neither a string nor None.

is_id_functions_consistent_ensembl(verbose=True)[source]

Check that the gene ids of the graph are those of Ensembl’s id tables, on every assembly at every release.

For each genome assembly and each release that the assembly has in the graph, the gene ids with their versions are read from the id table of that assembly and release (through the manager) and from the graph (the genes that the graph has on that assembly at that release, idtrack.TheGraph.trios()). The two sets must be equal: no gene of the table is missing in the graph and the graph has no gene that the table lacks.

Parameters:

verbose (bool) – Show a progress bar.

Returns:

details: compared (the number of assembly-release pairs), n_differing and differing (per differing pair its assembly and release, the numbers n_missing and n_extra, and the first ids missing in the graph and extra in it).

Return type:

CheckResult

is_id_functions_consistent_ensembl_2(verbose=True)[source]

Check that every gene version is referred to exactly at the releases of its history.

For every gene id with version of the backbone, two things the graph says independently must agree:

  1. The releases of its edges: the releases at which the gene is referred to (by its id without version, its transcripts, external identifiers) on the assembly that serves the release (idtrack.TheGraph.combined(), idtrack.TheGraph.serving_line). A gene that lived on an earlier assembly is referred to there at the releases that assembly served.

  2. The releases of its history: where Ensembl’s id history, validated against the id tables, has the version (idtrack.TheGraph.active_releases()).

Parameters:

verbose (bool) – Show a progress bar.

Returns:

details: compared (the number of gene versions), n_differing and differing (per gene its node and the release ranges edges and history).

Return type:

CheckResult

is_id_functions_consistent_external(verbose=True)[source]

Check that the external identifiers of the graph are those of Ensembl’s tables.

For each genome assembly and each release that the assembly has in the graph, and for every external database, the identifiers of the manager’s table of external identifiers (of every form of the graph) are compared with the identifiers the graph has for that database, assembly and release (idtrack.TheGraph.trios()). Both differences count: an identifier of the tables that the graph lacks, and an identifier of the graph that the tables do not have (the kind of error that produces wrong mappings). The graph keeps one node for identifiers that differ in letter case only, so the comparison ignores letter case; an identifier of the tables that is itself an Ensembl id of the graph is no external identifier there (misplaced_external_entry of the graph) and is left out.

Parameters:

verbose (bool) – Show a progress bar per assembly.

Returns:

details: compared (the number of database-assembly-release triples), n_differing and differing (per differing triple its database, assembly and release, the numbers n_missing and n_extra, and the first identifiers missing in the graph and extra in it, in lower case).

Return type:

CheckResult

is_node_consistency_robust(verbose=True)[source]

Check the two rules of the graph’s edges: no edge within a layer but the backbone’s, one edge between layers.

Beside the rule of is_edge_with_same_nts_only_at_backbone_nodes(), two nodes of different types are linked by exactly one edge: what the databases say about the pair at all releases is the content of that one edge (idtrack._the_graph.Connection). Several edges are allowed only between gene versions of the backbone (one per event of the history).

Parameters:

verbose (bool) – Show a progress bar.

Returns:

details: compared (the number of nodes), n_same_type and same_type as in is_edge_with_same_nts_only_at_backbone_nodes(), n_several_edges and several_edges (pairs of nodes of different types with more than one edge, with their types and the number of edges).

Return type:

CheckResult

is_range_functions_robust(verbose=True)[source]

Check that no two versions of one gene id are active at the same release.

The versions of a gene id follow one another in Ensembl’s history: at every release of the backbone an id has one version at most. For every gene id without version the release ranges of its versions on the backbone (idtrack.TheGraph.active_ranges()) are compared pair by pair; any release that two of them share is a violation.

Parameters:

verbose (bool) – Show a progress bar.

Returns:

details: compared (the number of gene ids), n_overlapping and overlapping (per pair the id, the two versions and the releases they share, as ranges).

Return type:

CheckResult

random_dataset_source_generator(assembly, include_external, include_ensembl, for_final_database, only_backbone_tests, release_lower_limit=None, form=None)[source]

Draw a database of a genome assembly and a release at which the graph has it.

The databases to draw from are chosen by the switches; of them only those that the graph has on the assembly at some release (at or after release_lower_limit, when that is given) can be drawn, and the release is one of theirs.

Parameters:

  • assembly (int) – The genome assembly.

  • include_external (bool) – External databases of the assembly can be drawn (synonyms excepted).

  • include_ensembl (bool) – Ensembl ids can be drawn: the gene ids of the backbone with and without version (ensembl_gene, base_ensembl_gene) and, unless for_final_database, the ids of the assembly (assembly_<key>_ensembl_<form>).

  • for_final_database (bool) – The draw is a target: the ids of one assembly are no target of a conversion.

  • only_backbone_tests (bool) – Draw ensembl_gene whatever the other switches say.

  • release_lower_limit (int | None) – The earliest release that can be drawn.

  • form (str | None) – Only databases that attach their ids to this form (gene, transcript, translation), and the Ensembl ids of this form.

Returns:

(database, assembly, release); None when none of the databases to draw from has a release that can be drawn.

Return type:

tuple[str, int, int] | None

Raises:

ValueError – If the switches leave no database to draw from (neither external databases nor Ensembl ids, and not the backbone alone).

class CheckResult(check, holds, details=<factory>)[source]

What one self-test of TrackTests found.

Every check (the methods whose names begin with is_) returns one. Its truth value is holds, so if tests.is_node_consistency_robust(): and assert tests.is_node_consistency_robust() mean what they say.

Parameters:

  • check (str)

  • holds (bool)

  • details (dict[str, Any])

check

The name of the check (the method).

Type:

str

holds

True when the invariant holds for the graph. False when a violation was found, and when the check could not be completed (then details has "error").

Type:

bool

details

What was compared and what was found: the counts of the things compared, and each kind of violation with its number and its first examples (at most idtrack.TrackTests.details_limit of them). For a check that could not be completed: "error" (the type and message of the exception) and "traceback".

Type:

dict[str, Any]
